UN-STARRED Question No. 3269 TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
 
Impact of Neem-Coated Urea 
 
3269. Shri Mahendra Singh Solanky: 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has made neem-coating of urea mandatory across the 
country, if so, the details and the objectives thereof; 
(b) the benefits achieved through neem-coated urea in improving nitrogen-use 
efficiency, reducing fertilizer misuse and enhancing crop productivity, 
particularly for farmers of the Dewas–Shajapur Parliamentary Constituency of 
Madhya Pradesh; 
(c) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding the impact of 
neem-coated urea in preventing diversion of subsidized urea for industrial and 
other non-agricultural purposes, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the quantity of neem-coated urea produced, supplied and marketed during the 
last three years, along with the details of allocation and distribution made to the 
State including the said Constituency, year-wise? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (c): It is mandatory for all the domestic producers and importers of Urea to supply 
100% Neem Coated Urea (NCU) since 2015 onwards.One of the primary benefits of 
Neem Coating is that due to slow release, the consumption of NCU reduces as compared 
to normal Urea, improving crop uptake, and reducing environmental losses. Research 
findings indicated that the average yield enhancement due to use of NCU is 8.25%. 
Further, application of NCU, significantly reduced the nitrogen losses by about 10%-15%. 
Neem-Coated Urea (NCU) acts as an effective nitrification inhibitors, leading to higher 
soil NH4+-N and lower NO2-N compared to prilled Urea, though their performance varies 
with soil type, crop, and region. Several studies have shown that NCU increases nitrogen 

availability, reduces NO3 leaching, and minimizes NH3 volatilization losses. Research 
across different soils consistently reports higher nitrogen recovery, improved yield at 
lower N application rates, and reduced nitrogen losses. 
The Government of India in consultation with the State Government is regularly 
monitoring the enforcement action taken by State Government against the cases of Black 
marketing, Hoarding, Sub-standard and Diversion on weekly basis. In the country, Since 
April 2026, 1,69,031 raids have been conducted with 9,127 show cause notices issued, 
2,868 licenses suspended/cancelled and 270 FIRs registered against defaulters. 
Additionally, in case of diversion 414 show cause notices issued, 113 licenses 
suspended/cancelled and 46 FIRs registered. This Ministry regularly pursue with the 
State Government to strictly implement the enforcement action against the defaulters. 
(d): The Quantum of Neem Coated Urea produced in the country during the last three 
years is as under: 
Year Production of Neem-Coated Urea (Fig. in LMT) 
2023-24 314.06 
2024-25 306.41 
2025-26 293.15 
Source: dbfert.nic.in 
In addition, following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring timely 
and adequate supply of fertilizers across the States/UTs, including the State of Madhya 
Pradesh: 
I. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise& month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
II. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
III. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other fertilizer 
is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in advance 
to ensure timely availability.  
IV. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
V. Regularly coordinate with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, 
priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 

VI. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
Accordingly, the availability of Urea has remained adequate in the State of Madhya 
Pradesh during the last three years (i.e. in FYs 2023-24 to 2025-26). The information 
regarding requirement, availability and sales of Urea in the State during the said period 
is placed at Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3270
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07TH AUGUST, 2026
VIOLATIONS OF FOOD SAFETY STANDARDS
3270. SHRI RAHUL GANDHI:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for the rising cases of food adulteration, contamination, counterfeiting and
repeated violations of food safety standards across the country;
(b) the details of food samples tested and found unsafe, prosecutions launched, convictions
secured, and the number of deaths due to food adulteration during the last five years, year
wise and State-wise;
(c) the details of food-testing infrastructure, including the number of functional laboratories,
the average testing time and vacancies of Food Safety Officers, State-wise;
(d) the number of notified FSSAI laboratories lacking facilities to test for heavy metals,
pesticide residues and bacterial contamination, along with the reasons therefor;
(e) whether any regulatory framework specifically governs storage conditions, temperature
control, hygiene, traceability and inspection frequency at quick-commerce dark stores, if so,
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and
(f) whether the Government proposes to launch a comprehensive National Food Safety
Mission to ensure food traceability, strengthen surveillance and safeguard public health, if so,
the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (f): Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is mandated to lay down
science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage,
distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human
consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act,
2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments.

Around 98% of the Food Business Operators (FBOs) fall within the jurisdiction of the
State/UT Food Safety Authorities. Accordingly, the enforcement and implementation of the
provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSS Act, 2006) primarily rests with the
State/UT Food Safety Authorities within their respective jurisdictions. For compliance with the
standards, limits, and other statutory requirements prescribed under the Food Safety and
Standards Act, 2006, and the regulations made thereunder, the State Food Safety Authorities
undertake surveillance, monitoring, targeted enforcement drives, inspections, and sampling
activities across the food sector.
Details of enforcement action taken by the State/UT Food Safety Authorities against non
-conforming food products (including adulteration) during the last 5 years (state wise) are
placed at Annexure-I.
For the quality and safety of the food and food products, FSSAI has notified 259 NABL
accredited food testing laboratories for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food
Laboratories for the analysis of appellate samples. These laboratories are notified for analysis of
food samples in accordance with their NABL-accredited scope. The Food analyst is required to
submit the report of analysis within fourteen days of receipt of the sample. State-wise details of
food testing laboratories are placed at Annexure-II.
Matters related to vacancies of Food Safety Officers (FSOs) in states are taken up
regularly with the Commissioner of Food Safety of States/UTs through Central Advisory
Committee (CAC) meetings. State-wise details of sanctioned strength, actual strength and
vacancies of Food Safety Officers, are attached as Annexure-III.
The number of FSSAI notified laboratories lacking the facilities to test heavy metals,
pesticides, microbiological parameters etc. are 13 across the country. In order to upgrade and
strengthen the testing infrastructure of State Food Testing Laboratories (SFTL), FSSAI has
provided financial and technical assistance for establishment of facilities for microbiological
analysis and procurement of High End Equipment (HEE) for heavy metals and pesticide
residues analysis.
FSSAI has specified General Hygienic and Sanitary Practices to be followed by
Licensed/Registered Food Business Operators under Schedule 4 of FSS (Licensing and
Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 which is applicable to all food business
operators including those involved in storage activity such as quick-commerce dark stores.
Schedule 4 of the said Regulations lays down the sanitary and hygienic requirements to be
complied with by Food Business Operators, including requirements relating to storage
conditions, temperature control, hygiene, transportation, pest control, personnel hygiene,
cleaning and sanitation, and maintenance of records to facilitate traceability, as applicable.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF LEGAL AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3271 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
REFORMS IN ARBITRATION LAW 
3271. SMT. ROOPKUMARI CHOUDHARY: 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any review of the implementation of the 
Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, with regard to achieving its objective of promoting 
speedy and efficient dispute resolution and reducing the burden on courts; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, including the major challenges identified in the implementation of 
the Act, particularly with regard to frequent judicial intervention and delays in arbitral 
proceedings; 
(c) whether the Government is considering any amendments to the Arbitration and Conciliation 
Act, 1996, to simplify procedures, minimise avoidable litigation arising out of arbitral 
proceedings and strengthen institutional arbitration in the country; 
(d) the steps taken to promote institutional arbitration, the capacity building of arbitrators, the 
adoption of technology and development of India as a preferred international arbitration hub; 
and 
(e) the measures proposed to ensure the time -bound enforcement of arbitral awards while 
maintaining minimal judicial intervention, in line with international best practices? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
 LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE INTHE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
(a) and (b) : During the past more than a decade, the Government,  inter-alia based on the 
recommendations of the 246th Report of the Law Commission of India and the report of the 
High Level Committee (HLC) chaired by Justice (Retd.) B. N. Srikrishna, Former Judge, 
Supreme Court of India, has progressively amended the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 
in the years 2015, 2019 and 2020, inter-alia to keep pace with developments in the arbitration 
landscape and to enable arbitration as a viable dispute resolution mechanism. The amendments 

2 
 
are aimed at ensuring timely conclusion of arbitration proceedings, neutrality of arbitrators, 
minimizing judicial intervention in the arbitral process, efficacious enforcement of arbitral 
awards and promotion of institutional arbitration. 
(c): Legislative and policy interventions including through amendments along with related 
reforms in the field of alternative dispute resolution including arbitration, is a continuous 
process, keeping in view the changing requirements of the stakeholders. Furth er, the 
interventions taken from time to time have contributed towards improving and strengthening 
the institutional arbitration landscape, making arbitration more efficacious and enabling the 
country being seen as an arbitration conducive jurisdiction.  
(d) and (e): The amendments made to the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, in the year 2019 
have enabled the statutory framework for institutional arbitration in India inter-alia through 
inclusion of Part IA in the Act. Further, the India International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019, 
was enacted to provide for the establishment of the India International Arbitration Centre for 
the purpose of creating an independent, autonomous and w orld class body for facilitating 
institutional arbitration and to declare the C entre to be an institution of national importance. 
The Centre has since been established and aims to inspire confidence amongst parties, both 
domestic and international, by providing a neutral dispute resolution platform for resolution of 
commercial disputes through arbitration. The Centre is envisaged to become a model arbitral 
institution in the country, thereby paving the way for enhancing the quality of institutional 
framework for arbitration. The Centre has also notified the India International Arbitra tion 
Centre (Conduct of Arbitration) Regulations, 2023 to facilitate conduct of domestic and 
international arbitrations, including through use of technology, with a focus on efficient and 
time-bound arbitration process.  Section 15 of the India Internation al Arbitration Centre Act, 
2019 also provides for the functions of the Centre and inter-alia states that the Centre shall 
impart training in alternative dispute resolution and related matters to those who are handling 
arbitration, conciliation and mediation. The Centre since its establishment, has conducted 
workshops, conferences and seminars rel ating to domestic and international arbitrations, for 
awareness and training where officials from Central Public Sector Enterprises and other 
stakeholders have participated. 
These legislative and policy interventions taken from time to time,  inter-alia 
including amendments made to Section 34 and 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 
in the year 2015 have contributed towards improving the arbitration ecosystem, minimizing 
judicial intervention in arbitration and better enforcement of arbitral awards thereby supporting 
the ease of doing business and enhancing investor confidence.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3272
TO BE ANSWERED ON 7TH AUGUST, 2026
WAITING LIST OF ORGAN TRANSPLANT
3272. SHRI KUNDURU RAGHUVEER:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware that a large number of patients suffering from end-stage
kidney failure remain on waiting lists for organ transplantation under programmes such as
Jeevandan and other organ allocation systems, resulting in avoidable deaths due to the
shortage of donor organs, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the number of patients currently awaiting kidney transplantation, the number of
transplants performed and the mortality reported among patients on waiting lists during the
last five years, year-wise and State-wise;
(c) whether the Government has assessed the gap between the demand for donor organs and
the availability of organs for transplantation, if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the Government proposes to intensify nationwide awareness campaigns, simplify
organ donation procedures and strengthen hospital-based organ retrieval programmes to
increase deceased organ donation, if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the measures taken by the Government to reduce transplant waiting periods and encourage
voluntary organ donation to save lives and improve access to organ transplantation?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (c) As per the provisions of the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act
(THOTA), 1994, and Rules made thereunder, respective State Governments are to ensure
compliance with respect to reporting of data by the transplant hospitals on the National Organ
and Tissue Transplant Registry (NOTTR) maintained by National Organ and Tissue

Transplant Organisation (NOTTO). As on 27th July, 2026, number of patients currently
awaiting kidney transplantation is 73,646. The States/UTs wise details of kidney transplants
performed and the number of patients who died while on waiting list for kidney transplant,
during the last five years are placed at Annexure-I and Annexure II respectively.
(d) & (e) Under the National Organ Transplant Programme (NOTP), funds are provided to
the States/UTs for augmentation of organ donation and transplantation including awareness
activities.
NOTTO along with Regional Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisations (ROTTOs) and
State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisations (SOTTOs) carries out awareness programs
across the country to disseminate information to promote organ and tissue donation engaging
with various stakeholders. Various awareness activities like poster making, slogan writing,
special pledge campaigns are organized regularly. The information about organ and tissue
donation including display of IEC materials are disseminated through the NOTTO website
www.notto.mohfw.gov.in. Also, a 24x7 call centre having a toll-free helpline number
(1800114770) is functional to provide information, tele-counselling and coordination for
organ donation. Dissemination of messages through social media platforms are also being
done on day-to-day basis. The citizens can take pledge for organ and tissue donation through
web portal https://notto.abdm.gov.in. As on date, more than 5 lakh Aadhaar verified pledges
have been registered.
In addition, a nationwide year-long public awareness campaign, “Jug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaan (जुग
जुग जजयो अजियान)” has been launched on 3rd August, 2026 with the aim to promote organ
and tissue donation. Further, the National Registry Portal has been upgraded and launched on
3rd August 2026 into a digital platform called e-पतारोपण (e-Pratyaaropan) to digitize organ
donation and transplantation processes, improve transparency and ensure smooth services to
the needy patients.

3273 SHRI LAXMIKANT PAPPU NISHAD:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has assessed the disparities in access to quality and affordable
healthcare in Uttar Pradesh, particularly in the Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar
districts and if so, the details thereof;
(b) the details of the sanctioned and vacant posts of doctors, specialists and paramedical
staff in District Hospitals, Community/ Primary Health Centres in the said district;
(c) the details of the healthcare infrastructure available in the said districts, including ICU
beds, trauma care facilities, diagnostic laboratories, dialysis units, CT and MRI facilities,
ambulances and maternal and child healthcare services;
(d) the details of the funds allocated, released and utilised under the National Health
Mission, Ayushman Bharat and other Central health schemes in the said districts during the
last five years; and
(e) whether the Government proposes to establish new medical colleges, upgrade District
Hospitals, strengthen specialist services and fill all vacancies in the said districts and if so,
the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a): ‘Public Health’ and ‘Hospital’ is a State subject, the primary responsibility for planning,
implementing, maintaining and to set up adequate number of healthcare facilities as per requirement
lies with the State Government. Under the National Health Mission (NHM), financial and technical
support is provided to States/UTs to strengthen their healthcare system based on proposals received
from States/UTs in their Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) within their resource envelop.
As per the information provided by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, the assessment of
health institutions, human resources, essential medicines, diagnostic facilities in all the districts
including Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar is done by State Government. Quality and
accessible health facilities are provided to the general public throughout the State including at the
medical units of Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar districts.

(b): As per Health Dynamics of India (HDI), 2023-24, the details regarding the availability of
doctors, specialists and paramedical staff in District Hospitals, Community/ Primary Health
Centres in Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar districts of Uttar Pradesh is available at
following link:
https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac62.pdf
(c): As per the Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM) Portal, 230 AAMs and 344 AAMs are operational
in Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar districts respectively. As per the Health Dynamics of India
(HDI) Report 2023–24, Sant Kabir Nagar district has 6 Community Health Centres (CHCs) and one
District Hospital, while Ambedkar Nagar district has 11 CHCs, one District Hospital, and one
Medical College. Adequate healthcare infrastructure is available at Sant Kabir Nagar and
Ambedkar Nagar districts, including ICU beds, trauma care facilities, diagnostic laboratories,
dialysis units, CT and MRI facilities, ambulances and maternal and child healthcare
services.
As per the information provided by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, Mahatma Jyotiba
Phule Joint District Hospital, Ambedkar Nagar, is equipped with 8 ICU beds, 10 Special
Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) beds, 6 trauma care beds, one Integrated Public Health
Laboratory (IPHL), a dialysis unit, one CT scan unit, two ultrasound machines, one digital
X-ray machine, one general X-ray machine, and a 100-bed Maternal and Child Health
(MCH) Wing.
Further, the State informed that ambulance services are operational in both districts
through the 108 Emergency Medical Transport Service (EMTS), with 23 and 26 ambulances
in Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar districts respectively, the Advanced Life Support
(ALS) Ambulance Service, with 6 and 5 ambulances in Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar
Nagar districts respectively, and the 102 Ambulance Service, with 21 and 26 ambulances in
Sant Kabir Nagar and Ambedkar Nagar districts respectively.
(d): The details of the Central Share released and utilised under the National Health Mission

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF PHARMACEUTICALS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †3274 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
 
Life-saving Medicines 
 
†3274. Shri Hanuman Beniwal:  
Shri Rajkumar Roat:  
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the increase in prices of essential and life -saving 
medicines has escalated the financial burden on common citizens, particularly patients 
belonging to low and middle-income groups and if so, the details of the price hike in medicines 
during the last three years, category-wise;  
(b) the steps taken by the Government to keep the prices of the said medicines affordable and 
to control unreasonable price increases during the last three years;  
(c) the number of cases of spurious, adulterated/Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) drugs that came 
to light in the country during the last three years, State-wise; and  
(d) the details of investigation, prosecution, license suspension/cancellation and other punitive 
actions taken by the Government against the concerned drug manufacturing companies, 
distributors and other defaulting entities in this regard? 
 
ANSWER  
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) and (b): Prices of drugs are regulated as per the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) 
Order 2013 (DPCO, 2013). The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) under the 
Department of Pharmaceuticals regulates the prices of medicines as per extant provisio ns of 
DPCO, 2013. NPPA fixes the ceiling prices of formulations specified in Schedule-I to DPCO, 
2013 which is based on the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) published by 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Mo HFW) from time -to-time. As on 23.07.2026, 
Ceiling prices of 935 formulations are effective. The average price reduction due to refixation 
of prices under NLEM, 2022 is about 17%. NPPA also fixes retail prices of new drugs as 
defined in para 2(1)(u) of DPCO, 2013, i.e., formulatio ns launched by existing manufacturers 
of a medicine listed in NLEM by combining it with another drug, or by changing the strength 
or dosage or both of such medicine. The retail prices of new drugs are applicable to the 
applicant manufacturer and marketer and they cannot sell the new drug above the price notified 
by NPPA. Retail prices of 3,845 new drugs have been fixed by the NPPA till 23.07.2026. 
Further, in case of non-scheduled formulations, manufacturers are required to not increase the 
maximum retail p rice (MRP) of a formulation by more than ten percent of the MRP of that 

formulation during the preceding 12 months.  In addition, NPPA has fixed the prices of drugs 
under Para 19 to ensure the availability of drugs at affordable prices in public interest. Details 
of prices fixed or revised by NPPA are available on NPPA’s website (www.nppa.gov.in). 
 
The ceiling prices of scheduled medicines are revised annually on the basis of 
Wholesale Price Index (WPI) (all commodities) for preceding calendar year on or before 1 st 
April of every year, which is notified by the Government on the 1 st day of April every year. 
This notified increase is the maximum permissible increase for schedule drug for that year, and 
a manufacturer may avail the same or a lower increase in the price of such drugs. The WPI of 
the last 3 years are as follows: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
In case of non-scheduled formulations, manufacturers may avail an increase of up to 10 
per cent in the MRP of a formulation over the MRP of that formulation during the preceding 
12 months. However, it is observed from the market data (based on Pharmarack database for 
June, 2026) that the weighted average annual price increase in the non-scheduled drugs over 
the last three years is 6.94% which is below the permissible price increase of 10% p.a. 
 
NPPA monitors the prices of both scheduled and non -scheduled formulations on an 
ongoing basis and takes action in accordance with the provisions of DPCO, 2013 against 
companies that are found overcharging consumers.  
 
Besides price regulation, Government has also enabled access to affordable essential 
medicines through Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), under which 
quality medicines are offered through Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) at rates that are typically 
50% to 80% lower than the prices of branded medicines.  In addition,  Under the Amrit 
(Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment) initiative of the Department of 
Health and Family Welfare, affordable medicines are provided for the treatment of cancer, 
cardiovascular and other diseases, implants, surgical dispo sables and other consumables etc., 
at an average discount of up to 50% on market rates through AMRIT Pharmacy stores set up 
in number of hospitals and healthcare institutions. Also, under the Free Drugs Service Initiative 
of the National Health Mission, essential medicines list recommended under the Indian Public 
Health Standards (IPHS) are made available free of any charge at public health facilities 
ranging from Primary Health Centres (PHCs) to district hospitals across the country.

CONSTITUTIONAL SAFEGUARDS OF UNDERTRIAL PRISONERS 
 
3275.  DR. GANAPATHY RAJKUMAR P:   
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Supreme Court has proposed a nationwide mechanism for daily judicial 
access inside prisons and has proposed a policy exploring under which court -appointed 
judges visit jails everyday to ensure that undertrial prisoners are not deprived of 
constitutional safeguards when they are not produced before the courts; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof ? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF  
LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
 
(a) & (b): The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) constituted under Legal Services 
Authorities Act, 1987 , whose Patron-in-Chief is the Chief Justice of India, is providing free 
and competent legal services to all undertrial prisoners and other inmates across the country. 
NALSA has taken several steps for providing free legal services/ assistance to the undertrial 
prisoners by way of Legal Services Clinics and Prison Legal Aid Clinics (PLACs) . The 
Secretary, District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), and the Chairman, DLSA (District & 
Sessions Judge), undertake periodic prison visits under the NALSA Standard Operating 
Procedure on Access to Legal Aid Services to Prisoners and Functioning of the Prison Legal 
Aid Clinics, 2022 (SOP - 2022), to ensure effective legal aid delivery and institutional 
oversight of prisoners . As mandated by the SOP, the Secretary, DLSA visits and inspect s 
every PLAC at least once every month and ensures that all eligible undertrial prisoners are 
provided legal representation, monitors prison conditions, review s instances of non -
production of prisoners before courts  and take immediate steps to address the lapses. There 
are dedicated Undertrial Review Committ ees (UTRCs) constituted at the district level to 
examine instances where undertrial prisoners are not produced before the Remand or Trial 
Court, whether physically or through video -conferencing, due to logistical or other 
constraints, and to recommend appropriate remedial measures.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No.3277  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
   
WORKING WOMEN HOSTELS IN ANDHRA PRADESH  
  
3277. DR. GUMMA THANUJA RANI:  
               
        Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
  
(a)  whether Government has reviewed the adequacy of Working Women Hostel facilities 
(WWH) in view of increasing migration of women for education, employment and 
industrial work in Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof;  
  
(b)  whether the Government has received any proposals from the said State for 
establishment/expansion of WWH outside Visakhapatnam district;  
  
(c)  if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken thereon; and  
  
(d)  the details of steps taken to ensure safety, affordability/accessibility of said hostels 
for working women?   
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
   
  
(a) to (d)  Sakhi Niwas Scheme [Working Women Hostel (WWH)] under the overarching 
Mission Shakti, is a demand driven centrally sponsored scheme where States/UTs assess their 
requirement as per local needs and their proposals are approved by the Programme Ap proval 
Board (PAB) after discussion with States/UTs. The Scheme aims to promote availability of 
safe and conveniently located accommodation for working women and for those women who 
are pursuing higher education and training, with Day care facility for chi ldren in urban, semi -
urban and even rural areas where employment opportunity for women exists.   In this scheme, 
fund is provided for rental accommodation and component of construction  has been 
discontinued.  Funds under the Scheme are released to the State s/UTs in accordance with the 
guidelines of the Department of Expenditure through the Single Nodal Agency (SNA)/SNA -
SPARSH mechanism of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).   
  

Presently, 23 Sakhi Niwas(WWH) are operational in the State of Andhra Pradesh.  The 
details of the operational Sakhi Niwas in the State of Andhra Pradesh are given at Annexure -I. 
  
           Further, under Part (X) – Construction of Working Women Hostels of the Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) Scheme, an amount of ₹172.00 crore was 
allocated to the Government of Andhra Pradesh. The State Government submitt ed three 
proposals for the construction of Working Women Hostels in Visakhapatnam district, with a 
total project cost of ₹172.00 crore. These proposals were approved by the Department of 
Expenditure, and the first instalment of ₹113.52 crore was released t o the State Government 
during 2024–25. The details of the approved proposals are given at Annexure -II. 
  
To ensure the safety, affordability and accessibility of Working Women Hostels, 
secure accommodation is provided with boundary walls, security personnel, CCTV 
surveillance, biometric access/visitor registers, and adequate lighting, wherever applicable. 
Basic amenities such as furnished rooms, safe drinking water, sanitation, electricity, internet 
connectivity, and common facilities are also provided.   The Ministry also continuously 
monitors the implementation of the Scheme through physical and virtual review meetings with 
States/UTs, field visits by Ministry officials, and digital monitoring mechanisms. Based on the 
findings, appropriate measures are taken, and advisories are issued to States/UTs from time to 
time to facilitate effective implementation of th e Scheme.

CENTRAL ADOPTION RESOURCE AUTHORITY  
 
3279.  SHRI P P CHAUDHARY: 
SHRI P C MOHAN: 
SHRI BHOJRAJ NAG: 
SHRI VIJAY KUMAR DUBEY:  
SHRI MANISH JAISWAL: 
SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY:  
SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:  
DR. HEMANT VISHNU SAVARA:  
SMT. ANITA NAGARSINGH CHOUHAN:  
DR. HEMANG JOSHI: 
SHRI NABA CHARAN MAJHI:  
SHRI NALIN SOREN: 
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)    whether the Government has taken any new initiative through the Central Adoption 
Resource Authority (CARA) to make the adoption process, more transparent, simplified 
and timebound in the country;  
(b)    if so, the details thereof;  
(c)     the number of children adopted through CARA in the country during the last two years, 
along with the average waiting period for adoption, State/UT -wise including Rajasthan, 
Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra;  
(d)    whether the Government proposes to increase the number of Specialised Adoption 
Agencies (SAAs)/strengthen the necessary facilities for the rehabilitation of abandoned 
and orphaned children in the country, if so, the details thereof along with the es timated 
timeline in this regard State/UT-wise and constituency -wise; 
(e)    the details of the measures taken to reduce the average time taken for completion of 
adoption process; and 
(f)     the details of the steps proposed to expand awareness and outreach services in the country? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (f):.  The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal Ministry for the 
administration of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act, 2015), 
the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Model Rules, 2016 and the Adopt ion 
Regulations, 2022 for adoption through the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA). 
Under the JJ Act 2015, the Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) have been empowered to take 

decisions with regard to the children in need of care and protection including orphaned, 
abandoned and surrendered.  
  
The District Magistrate has been empowered to issue Adoption Orders as per Section 58(3) 
and Section 61 of the JJ Act, 2015 read with Regulation 36 of Adoption Regulations, 2022. 
As per Schedule XIV of the Adoption Regulations 2022, timelines have been defined for each 
stakeholder.  
  
The waiting period of the Prospective Adoptive Parents (PAPs) depends on the availability of 
children who are declared legally free for adoption by CWC. It also depends on the choice of 
the PAPs to adopt from the age group preferred.  
  
In order to reduce delays and to maintain transparency, CARA has digitized end -to-end 
process through the digital platform of Adoption Module under Mission Vatsalya portal  and 
regular monitoring and follow -ups is done with the State Governments and UT 
Administrations including all stakeholders to expedite the process, as per the Schedule XIV 
of the Adoption Regulation, 2022 which has stipulated timeline for authorities and agencies 
working in adoption. 
  
The Ministry is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely ‘Mission Vatsalya’ in 
all States and Union Territories on predefined cost sharing basis between the Central and the 
State Governments to deliver various services for children in difficult circumstances including 
orphan children. The scheme provides institutional care and non-institutional care. Child Care 
Institutions (CCIs) established under the Mission Vatsalya scheme provide, inter -alia, age -
appropriate education, access to vocational train ing, recreation, health care, counselling etc. 
The Scheme also supports the Specialized Adoption Agencies (SAAs) registered under the 
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act,2015, where adoptable children of 
below six years of age are provid ed residential care.  
  
States and UTs have been advised to establish at least one Specialised Adoption Agency 
(SAA) in each district in accordance with Sections 65 and 66 of the JJ Act, 2015, read with 
Adoption Regulations, 2022 (Regulations 3 & 5). 795 SAAs have been approved u nder 
Mission Vatsalya Scheme for all State Governments and Union Territory Administrations as 
on 29.07.2026. All SAAs are mandatorily onboarded onto the integrated CARINGS -Mission 
Vatsalya system, enabling end -to-end digital processing of adoption cases in cluding referral, 
matching, and documentation. Compliance is monitored through real -time dashboards at 
Central and State levels, and through periodic review meetings.  
  
The nationwide Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities as well as 
localized outreach programmes to promote adoption and foster care are conducted under 
Mission Vatsalya. CARA also undertakes awareness and outreach activities across the 
country to create awareness and promote legal adoption including workshops, seminars and 
orientation sessions for stakeholders. Awareness regarding legal adoption procedures and the 
importance of child adoption through print, electronic and social media plat forms, etc is also 
undertaken regularly by CARA.  
  
States and UTs Administration wise detail of children adopted through CARA in the country 
during the last two years including Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra 
is at Annexure.

SAGARMALA PROGRAMME 
  
3280. SMT. BHARTI PARDHI:  
 SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR:  
 SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE:  
 SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE:  
 DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE:  
  
Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state:

(a) the total financial and technical assistance sanctioned by the Union 
Government during the current year under the 'Sagarmala Programme' to construct 
new jetties and passenger terminals along the eastern and western coasts of Mumbai; 
  
(b) whether these water transport projects will alleviate overcrowding on roads and 
suburban railways, thereby saving travel time and money for the general public;  
  
(c) the details of the policy of the Union Government to ensure that the ticket fares 
remain affordable for ordinary citizens;  
  
(d) the specific financial provisions made to empower the traditional business of 
the local Koli community and fishermen through modern jetties without causing any 
disruption to their livelihoods; and  
  
(e) the current status of projects undertaken to expand Ro-Ro (Roll-on/Roll-off) 
and passenger ferry services in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a): On account of non-availability of fiscal space in the current Sagarmala scheme, 
no new project for construction of jetties and passenger terminals along the eastern 
and western coasts of Mumbai has been sanctioned in the current financial year.  

  
(b): Under the current Sagarmala Scheme, 18 Ro-Ro / Ro-Pax infrastructure 
projects worth ₹ 561 crore have been sanctioned in the state of Maharashtra to 
improve coastal connectivity. Development of water transport infrastructure, including 
passenger jetties, ferry terminals and Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax facilities, promotes coastal 
shipping and inland water transport as sustainable and efficient modes of transport. 
These projects provide an alternative mode of passenger and vehicular movement, 
thereby reducing pressure on congested roads and suburban rail networks, reducing 
travel time, fuel consumption and logistics costs, while contributing to environmental 
sustainability. 
  
(c): The Central Government provides financial assistance under Sagarmala 
scheme for development of water transport infrastructure. As per the notification 
no.12/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28.06.2017, transportation of passengers, with 
or without accompanied belongings, by public transport, other than predominantly for 
tourism purpose, in a vessel between places located in India is exempted from GST. 
The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) has also exempted port & 
vessel related charges for the Ro-Pax and passenger ferry operations till 22.01.2027. 
  
(d): Government of Maharashtra has informed that the Department of Fisheries is 
undertaking the development of modern fishing jetties and allied infrastructure to 
strengthen the traditional livelihoods of the Koli community and fishermen. The details 
of financial assistance provided by MoPSW under the Sagarmala scheme for fishing 
harbours / fish landing centres in the state of Maharashtra is available at Annexure 1. 
  
(e): Under Sagarmala Scheme, in the state of Maharashtra 18 Ro-Ro / Ro-Pax 
infrastructure projects worth ₹ 561 crore have been sanctioned to improve coastal 
connectivity. Out of these, 13 projects worth ₹ 340 crore are completed in the state of 
Maharashtra. The details are available at Annexure 2. No Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax/ferry projects 
have been sanctioned in the state of Madhya Pradesh under Sagarmala scheme.

DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3281 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
 
PENDENCY OF CASES IN MUMBAI COURTS 
 
3281. SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL:  
 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the pendency of civil, criminal 
and commercial cases in courts functioning in Mumbai during the last three years, particularly 
in view of the city's importance as the financial and commercial capital of the country;  
 
(b) the details of financial assistance, infrastructure projects and technological initiatives 
undertaken by the Central Government for strengthening judicial infrastructure, the 
construction of court complexes, the establishment of additional courts and the implementation 
of e-Courts projects in Mumbai;  
 
(c) whether the Government has identified shortages of judicial officers, courtrooms, digital 
infrastructure and support staff affecting the timely disposal of cases in Mumbai, if so, the 
details of action taken/proposed to be taken in this regard; and  
 
(d) the measures taken or proposed to reduce pendency, strengthen judicial infrastructure, 
expand digital court services and improve access to speedy and affordable justice for litigants 
in Mumbai?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a): The details of pendency of civil, criminal and commercial cases in courts functioning in 
Mumbai during the last three years are at Annexure. 
 
(b): The primary responsibility for development of infrastructure facilities for District and 
Subordinate Courts rests with the State Governments/UTs. However, to augment the resources 
of States/UTs, Central Government has been implementing a Centrally Sponsore d Scheme 
(CSS) for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for Judiciary in the District and 

2 
Subordinate Courts since 1993 -94, by providing financial assistance in the prescribed fund 
sharing pattern between the Centre and States/UTs. Financial assistance of Rs. 1127.89 cr has 
been released to the State of Maharashtra under the scheme since its inception. In the current 
financial year, a tentative allocation of Rs. 27.05 cr has been made for the State of Maharashtra, 
out of which Mother Sanction for an amount of Rs. 13.525 cr has been issued.  
 
The High Court of Bombay and all working courts in Mumbai have been equipped with 
the necessary ICT infrastructure as provisioned under the eCourts Project.  Further, 13 eSewa 
Kendras have been established in Mumbai City and equipped with essential infrastructure. An 
amount of Rs. 104.32 crore has been released to the High Court of Bombay under the eCourts 
Project in the FY 2025 -26. The High Court of Bombay has also established 6 Online Courts 
and 6 Paperless Courts which are equipped with the necessary ICT infrastructure  to facilitate 
efficient paperless and digital court proceedings. 
 
(c) & (d): The Government of Maharashtra vide letter 07.02.2025 sanctioned 2863 new posts 
of Judicial Officers for State of Maharashtra taking the sanctioned strength to 5247. 
Disposal of cases pending in various courts lies within the domain of the Judiciary. 
Disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter-alia, include availability of 
adequate number of Judges and Judicial officers, supporting court staff, physical infrastructure, 
complexity of facts involved, quality of investigation, nature of evidence, co-operation of stake 
holders viz bar, investigation agencies, witnesses, litigants. However, the Government is fully 
committed for speedy disposal of cases and reducing pendency. The Government has taken 
several initiatives to provide an ecosystem for faster disposal of cases by the judiciary which, 
inter-alia, involves timely appointment of Judges, better infrastructure for courts including 
computerization, policy and legislative measures in the areas prone to excessive litigation, 
promoting Alternate Dispute Resolution mechanism, enactment and implementation of New 
Criminal Laws 2023, establishment of Fast Track Special Courts, re-engineering of court 
procedure and emphasis on human resource development. 
In addition, t he State Courts Management System (SCMS) Committee of Hon'ble 
Bombay High Court has been preparing Action Plan on yearly basis since November 2017 for 
speedy disposal of old cases pending before Courts of District Judiciary. This Action Plan aims 
to dispose of old cases in speedy manner. The said Action Plan also focus on fixed timelines 
for disposal of cases and holding regular meetings with Advocates, Bar Association, Senior 
police officers/Pubic Prosecutors, Senior Nodal Of ficer from Revenue Department for quick 
disposal of old cases. 
Further, in order to provide legal assistance and representation in courts to marginalized 
and disadvantaged sections of society, 845 advocates from the Bar Council of Maharashtra and 
Goa have been registered as Pro Bono lawyers under the Nyaya Bandhu Programme,  as on 
31.07.2026.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3282 
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
  
DAMAGE TO EMBANKMENTS IN SUNDERBANS DUE TO CARGO SHIP 
MOVEMENT 
 
3282. SHRI BAPI HALDAR: 
 
       Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पƣन, पोत पǐरवहन और जलमाग[ मंğी 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that the frequent movement of large cargo 
vessels through the inland waterways of the Sundarbans delta is causing severe 
erosion and damage to riverbank embankments in districts such as South 24 
Parganas, including the Mathurapur region; 
(b) whether any study has been undertaken to assess the ecological and structural 
impact of heavy ship traffic on small islands such as Mousuni, Ghoramara, Kumirmari, 
Satjelia, Chhotomollakhali and Amtoli that are facing existential threats due to 
embankment breaches, saline water ingress and wave pressure; 
(c)   if so, the details thereof and the corrective steps taken by the Government in this 
regard; and 
(d) whether the Government is considering either limiting or regulating the cargo 
movement through ecologically fragile zones or allocating special funds under 
Sagarmala or any other scheme for long-term protection and fortification of 
embankments, if so, the details thereof?  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
 (a)       Riverbank erosion is a complex natural phenomenon influenced by several 
factors, including river morphology, sediment transport, hydrological regime, tidal 
action, bank material and local hydraulic conditions. Inland Waterways Authority of 
India (IWAI), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and 
Waterways (MoPSW) undertakes only navigational interventions for maintenance of 
fairways in only 30-45 meter channel of the river and no specific evidence has been 
established indicating that movement of shallow-draft Inland Water Transport (IWT) 

vessels operating on National Waterway (NW)-97 (Sundarbans Waterways) has 
caused riverbank or embankment erosion. Fairway maintenance activities are planned 
keeping in view navigational requirements and applicable environmental safeguards.   
  
(b) & (c)  No dedicated study has been undertaken by IWAI and Govt. of West Bengal 
to establish a direct correlation between IWT operations and riverbank erosion in NW-
97. However, IWAI carries out periodic hydrographic surveys and continuous 
monitoring of channel conditions for maintenance of navigable fairways. The 
hydrographic data, together with river behaviour and navigational requirements, forms 
the basis for planning and implementation of fairway maintenance measures. 
  
(d)  IWAI regulates the movement of vessels through ecologically fragile zones with 
following measures:  
 Restricting  speed of the vessels within the sanctuary. 
 Fitting vessels with propeller guards and dolphin deflectors. 
 Restricting navigation to designated channels. 
 Using non-toxic anti-fouling paints. 
MoPSW has not allocated  special funds under Sagarmala or any other scheme for 
long-term protection and fortification of embankments.

UNUTILISED FUND UNDER NPRD 2021
3284. SHRI JOYANTABASUMATARY:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has taken a formal decision regarding unutilised funds under
National Policy for Rare Diseases (NPRD) 2021 for the current and previous financial years,
if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;
(b) whether these funds are proposed to be carried forward, reallocated or allowed to lapse, if
so, the details thereof including the quantum of funds proposed to be carried forward,
reallocated and allowed to lapse along with the reasons for each of the same and the rules
governing such decisions;
(c) whether the Government is likely to permit immediate utilisation of unspent funds to
support patients who have exhausted the one-time assistance, if so, the details thereof and if
not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether the Government accepts responsibility for the denial of treatment despite the
availability of funds in this regard, if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the time-bound measures being taken by the Government to ensure full utilisation of funds
meant for life-saving care?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (d) The National Policy for Rare Diseases (NPRD), 2021 has utilized
approximately 98.80% of the Revised Estimate (RE) for FY 2023-24, 97.60% for FY 2024-
25 and 98.90% for FY 2025-26. In FY 2026-27, around 39.08% of the Budget Estimate (BE)
has already been utilized as on date. The lumpsum funds released to the Centers of
Excellence (CoEs) based on the recommendation of the dedicated Rare Disease Committee at
each CoE after clinical examination of the patients on case-to-case basis are carried forward
to the next year.

The matter of providing financial assistance above the ceiling of ₹50 lakhs under NPRD is
sub judice before Hon’ble Supreme Court, wherein the Government has been directed to
comply with the extant guidelines of the policy.
(e) Some of the measures taken by the Government to ensure full utilization of funds
under NPRD are:
 The number of Rare Diseases identified under NPRD has increased from 51 to 63,
enabling more patients to get benefit under the policy.
 The number of Centers of Excellence (CoEs) has doubled from 8 to 16 since the
inception of the policy in 2021, thereby increasing geographical outreach and
accessibility of treatment.
 The guidelines of the policy have been amended to enable the CoEs to outsource
transplant facilities to fast track the treatment of patients suffering from Group 1 Rare
Diseases.

QUALITY OF GENERIC MEDICINES
†3286. SMT. SANJNA JATA V:
DR. RAJKUMAR SANGWAN:
SHRI RAHUL KASWAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study regarding the present status of
prescribing generic medicines by the Government and private medical practitioners along
with the proportion of patients purchasing medicines from JAKs, State-wise particularly in
the Bharatpur Parliamentary Constituency of Rajasthan, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether several patients still have misconception and mistrust regarding the quality of
generic medicines in the said district, if so, the details thereof along with the concrete steps
taken by the Government to enhance public trust in this regard; and
(c) whether the Government proposes to effectively integrate the Jan Aushadhi Pariyojana
with Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB- PMJAY), Government
hospitals, e-health systems and digital prescription mechanisms, district-wise particularly in
the said constituency, if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (c): Clause 1.5 of the Indian Medical Council (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and
Ethics) Regulations, 2002 provides that every physician should prescribe drugs with generic
names legibly and preferably in capital letters and he/she shall ensure that there is a rational
prescription and use of drug. Further, the Directorate General of Health Services has
instructed vide order dated 12.05.2023 that all doctors in Central Government hospitals,
CGHS Wellness Centres and polyclinics prescribe generic medicines.
Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) are retail outlets selling medicines directly to the customers. An
estimated 15 lakh citizens visit the JAKs located across the entire country on a daily basis.
State/UT-wise details of sale under Jan Aushadhi Scheme during F.Y .2025-26 is available at
Annexure. Separate data on the number of beneficiaries availing medicines from JAKs in
Bharatpur Parliamentary Constituency of Rajasthan is not maintained centrally.

Stringent measures as specified below are in place to ensure that the medicines supplied
through Jan Aushadhi Kendras meet standards:
i. Medicines are procured only from suppliers certified for World Health
Organization – Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP).
ii. Each batch of drugs supplied under the scheme is tested at laboratories
accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration
Laboratories (NABL) and only after passing quality tests, medicines are
dispatched to Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
iii. Quality audit of the facilities of vendors is routinely done by the
Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India.
To promote acceptability and to increase sale of medicines supplied through JAKs, targeted
awareness campaigns about the benefits of Janaushadhi medicines are conducted on a regular
basis:
 Multi-channel awareness campaigns: Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of
India (PMBI) conducts regular awareness campaigns through print, television, radio,
social media, outdoor publicity, and community outreach in collaboration with
organizations such as the Central Bureau of Communication, PIB, MyGov, and MY
Bharat to promote the benefits of Jan Aushadhi medicines.
 Citizen outreach and stakeholder engagement: Awareness is enhanced through
WhatsApp chatbots, outbound calls, Jan Aushadhi Week activities (including health
camps, rallies, seminars, and public engagement programmes), and audio/video
messages from eminent public representatives and doctors to build trust and dispel
myths about the quality of Jan Aushadhi medicines.
 Focused rural outreach: Special campaigns in rural areas, including health camps,
nukkad-natak, audiovisual displays at Common Service Centres, and workshops in
local languages in association with Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs), are conducted to
improve awareness, acceptability, and uptake of Jan Aushadhi medicines.
Also, a mobile application “Jan Aushadhi Sugam” is a facility for the general public that
provides a digital platform to avail user-friendly services like- locating nearby JAK,
availability of Janaushadhi medicines, product comparison of generic vs branded medicine in
the form of MRP saving, etc. The Jan Aushadhi Sugam App has been onboarded on the
Arogya Setu 2.0 platform of the AB-PMJAY .
Further, under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), eligible
beneficiary families are provided cashless health insurance coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per
family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. The Health Benefit Packages
(HBPs) notified under the scheme are comprehensive bundled packages that cover the entire
continuum of treatment, including pre-hospitalization expenses for up to 3 days,
hospitalization costs such as diagnostics, medicines, implants (where applicable), and
consumables, as well as post-hospitalization care for up to 15 days, including medicines and
follow-up consultations.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3287 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
Timely Availability of Fertilizers 
 
3287.  Dr. Alok Kumar Suman: 
                
Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding the availability 
of fertilizers to farmers across the country, if so, the details of production, allocation 
and distribution of major fertilizers during the last three years, State-wise and year-
wise; 
 
(b) whether any shortage of fertilizers has been reported, if so, the details thereof 
along with the corrective measures taken thereon; 
 
(c) the details of subsidies provided on fertilizers during the said period; 
 
(d) the steps taken to promote balanced and efficient use of fertilizers and 
encourage alternative nutrient sources; and 
 
(e)  the timeline fixed by the Government to ensure timely availability of fertilizers to 
farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
 

(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient 
rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has 
remained adequate in the country during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. The State-
wise information regarding availability position of these fertilizers in last 3 years and 
during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season (as on 03.08.2026) is placed at Annexure.

country during last 3 years 2023-24 to 2025-26 is as under:

Further, the Government is promoting sustainable and balanced use of fertilizers 
through judicious use of synthetic fertilizers, adopting alternate fertilizers, promoting 
organic/natural farming and implementing resource conservation technologies. Soil test 
based recommendations in conjunction with organic fertilizer and bio-fertilizers is holds 
the key for balanced used of fertilizers. Further, the Government is implementing various 
schemes such as National Mission on Natural Farming, Paramparagat Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PKVY), Namami Gange, Bhartiya Prakritik Krishi Padhati (BPKP), Mission 
Organic Value Chain Development for North- Eastern Region (MOVCDNER), National 

Project on Organic Farming (NPOF) etc., farmers are provided assistance for use of 
organic and bio-fertilizers. Further, National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming 
(NCONF) is involved in awareness generation & training activities for promotion of organic 
farming. Achieving balanced fertilization requires a multi-pronged strategy that 
integrates policy, technology, and farmer participation. The following measures have 
been adopted for balanced use of fertilizers: 
 
i. Balanced use of fertilizer is promoted under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, 
being implemented since 2014-15. Under the scheme, Soil Health Cards (SHCs) 
are generated which provide nutrient status of soil, based on which crop-wise 
fertilizer recommendations are provided to farmers, thereby promoting balanced 
and efficient nutrient management. SHC helps in enhancing crop productivity, 
reduce cultivation costs, and promote sustainable agriculture. So far, 26.09 crore 
Soil Health Cards have been generated and issued to farmers. 130627 farmer’s 
trainings, 7.17 lakh demonstrations, 7425 farmer’s Melas/ campaigns on soil health 
card recommendations have been organized across the country.  
ii. National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved by the Union Cabinet 
on 25 November 2024.  NMNF promotes chemical-free, nature-based farming 
practices using on-farm inputs. Under the scheme, 23.13 lakh farmers have been 
registered and 11.44 lakh hectares area have been covered,  
iii. Special awareness Campaign and Khet Bachao Abhiyan  on balanced use of 
fertilizers have been conducted by Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
(DA&FW) and ICAR during the current Kharif Season 2026 wherein total  2,94,554 
programs covering 1,36,73,465 farmers have been achieved. During the 
campaign, farmers have also been made aware on Natural/Organic Farming, bio-
inputs, alternative fertilizers etc.  
iv. Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is implemented since 2015-16.  PKVY 
promotes organic farming by providing end-to-end support covering production, 
processing, certification, and marketing. So far, 18.93 lakh hectares have been 
brought under organic farming and 33.63 lakh farmers have been benefited. 
v. Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region 
(MOVCDNER) is implemented since 2015-16 to promote organic farming in North 
Eastern States.  So far, 2.36 lakh hectares have been brought under organic 
farming and 2.74 lakh farmers have been benefited.  
vi. The Government also promotes Soil Organic Carbon Enhancer namely, 
Fermented Organic Manure (FOM) /Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) as 
a part of judicious use of fertilizers. During 2024-25, the annual consumption of 
FOM/LFOM was 3.36 LMT. During the current Kharif Season (1.4.2026 to 
16.7.2026), the consumption of FOM/LFOM  is 11.86 LMT. 
 
Besides, the Government has approved Market Development Assistance (MDA) 
Scheme (FY 2023-24 to 2025-26) under which assistance @ Rs. 1500/MT is being 
provided to CBG plants/Fertilizer Marketing Companies for promotion of organic carbon 
enhancers, viz., Fermented Organic Manure (FOM)/Liquid Fermented Organic Manure 
(LFOM) and organic fertilizer, viz., Phosphate Rich Organic Manure (PROM) produced 
at plants under GOBARdhan initiative, with total outlay of Rs.1451.84 Crore (FY 2023-
24 to 2025-26), which includes, a corpus of Rs. 360 Crore for research gap funding, etc. 
 

These initiatives of the Government are expected to address the imbalanced use of 
chemical fertilizers thereby reducing chemical fertilizer use.

Moreover, In order to promote the use of Nano Fertilizers among farmers across 
the country, the following measures have been undertaken by the Government: 
 
• Use of Nano Fertilizers is promoted through different activities such as awareness 
camps, webinars, field demonstrations, Kisan Sammelans and films in regional languages 
etc. 
• Nano Fertilizers, like Nano Urea and Nano DAP, are made available at Pradhan 
Mantri Kisan Samridhi Kendras (PMKSKs) by concerned companies. 
• For ease in application and utilization of Nano fertilizers, like Nano Urea and Nano 
DAP, through foliar application, initiatives such as innovative spraying options like 'Kisan 
Drones' and distribution of battery operated sprayers at retail points are undertaken. For 
this purpose, pilot training and custom hiring spraying services through Village Level 
Entrepreneurs are actively promoted. 
 
   In addition to this, Kisan Sangoshthis are conducted by the fertilizer companies 
for extensive field interaction with farmers, local farmer cooperatives, panchayats etc. 24 
Fertilizer Marketing Companies (FMCs) conducted 23,389 Camps/Kisan Sangoshthis 
across the Country during February 2025 to June 2026 . Camps/Kian Sangoshthis are 
being organised for promotion of FOM/LFOM/PROM under PM-PRANAM by the Fertilizer 
companies. This initiative focuses on critical areas such as balanced use of fertilizers, 
integrated nutrient management (INM), promotion of organic farming, and soil health 
improvement. Awareness activities for farmers include demonstrations on the application 
of FOM, LFOM, PROM, Potash Derived from Molasses (PDM). This camps also feature 
technical sessions on appropriate fertilizer dosages, crop-specific application techniques, 
and the benefits of organic inputs. The program aims to enhance farmers understanding 
of INM, encourage adoption of balanced nutrient practices, and strengthen outreach and 
credibility through demonstration plots and interactive farmer engagement. The 
Government is regularly coordinating with State and Union Territory Governments to 
support and promote their efforts under this scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3289 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
Distribution of Fertilizers in Karnataka 
 
3289. Shri P C Mohan: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Bharat brand fertilizers under the One Nation One Fertilizer initiative are 
being distributed in Karnataka and if so, the details thereof along with the quantity of 
Bharat Urea, Bharat DAP, Bharat MOP and Bharat NPK supplied to the said State 
during the last two years, year-wise; 
 
(b) the number of fertilizer companies, State Trading Entities and Fertiliser Marketing 
Entities distributing fertilisers under the Bharat brand in the said State; 
 
(c) whether the criss-cross movement of fertilizers has reduced in the said State, if 
so, the details thereof along with the benefits accrued to farmers; and 
 
(d) whether the current availability position of fertilizers in the said State is sufficient 
to meet the requirement for Kharif season 2026, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (d) One Nation One Fertilizer scheme stands implemented under 
"Pradhanmantri Bhartiya Janurvarak Pariyojna" (PMBJP) with effect from 24th 
August, 2022. All fertilizers companies viz Public sector, Cooperative and Private 
sector are required to sell subsidized fertilizers under brand name "BHARAT" across 
the country. The objective of the scheme is to increase the availability basket of 
fertilizers; take care of dilemma among farmers in choosing from plethora of brands 
manufactured by various companies available in the markets, reduce the crisscross 
movement and further ensure timely supply of fertilizers across the country, including 
the State of Karnataka. By consolidating branding under a single "BHARAT" brand, 
the scheme fosters transparency, combats malpractices, and ensures equitable 
access to essential nutrients for crops. 
Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, assesses 

 
the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of requirement 
projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of 
fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and continuously monitors the 
availability. 
Accordingly, the available of fertilizers, viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has remained 
adequate in the State of Karnataka during the last two years and ongoing Kharif 2026 
season. The information regarding the requirement, availability and sales of said 
fertilizers in the State during the last two years is placed at Annexure-A and ongoing 
season is placed at Annexure-B. 
Moreover, the major fertilizer suppliers/companies operating in the State of 
Karnataka are GSFC, IFFCO, KRIBHCO, MFL, PPL, RCF, RFCL, SPIC, FACT, IPL, 
CIL, GFL, STL, NBCL and NFL.

UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 3290

REVIEW OF THE PROHIBITION OF CHILD MARRIAGE (AMENDMENT) BILL, 
2021 
3290. DR. Shashi Tharoor: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government received any report, recommendations/other material from the 
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, 
Children, Youth and Sports arising out of its examination of the Prohibition of Child 
Marriage (Ame ndment) Bill, 2021 before the Bill lapsed with the dissolution of the 
17th Lok Sabha;  
(b)  if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether the Government has undertaken any fresh review/stakeholder consultations on 
raising the minimum age of marriage for women to 21 years, if so, the details thereof; 
and  
(d)  whether the Government proposes to reintroduce the proposal, taking into account the 
inputs received during the Committee's examination, if so, the details along with the 
timeline thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD  DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
 
  
(a) and (b): The Government introduced 'the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 
2021’ in the Parliament on 21.12.2021.   The Bill was referred to the Department Related 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth and Sp orts for 
examination. Consequent upon the dissolution of 17th Lok Sabha, the aforesaid Bill lapsed.  

No report was received from the Committee. However, during the Committee's examination of 
the Bill, some memoranda were received from the Committee  seeking comments from this 
Ministry, to which responses were furnished by the Ministry to the Committee.  
(c) and (d): The Government reviews the laws, policies and programmes from time to time and 
takes appropriate measures, based on the experience gathered during the implementation and 
feedback received from stakeholders.

(a) the number of countries with which India has signed Memoranda of  
Understanding or cooperation agreements for Digital Public Infrastruc -
ture (DPI), along with the key areas of cooperation;
(b) the key details of all such agreements;
(c) the progress made in the implementation of these agreements, in -
cluding the deployment of India's digital public goods and capacity-build-
ing initiatives in partner countries;
(d) the institutional framework adopted for coordinating DPI partner -
ships with partner countries and the concerned Ministries and agencies;  
and
(e) the roadmap for expanding India's international cooperation on Di -
gital  Public  Infrastructure,  particularly  with  countries  of  the  Global 
South for the next three years?

2
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a) The framework inter-Governmental Memorandum of Understanding  
(MoU) on Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), titled “Cooperation in the  
Field of Sharing Successful Digital Solutions Implemented at Population  
scale for Digital Transformation” has been signed with 24 countries till  
date to facilitate the exchange of experiences, best practices, and India  
Stack technology solutions.
(b) The key objective of  the framework MoU on DPI is to advance  
digital  transformation  for  the  benefit  of  partner  countries  through 
capacity  building  for  public  officials,  exchange  of  best  practices, 
development of  pilot solutions, facilitation of  private sector contacts,  
among others.
(c) The  Government  regularly  facilitates  study  visits  and  technical 
interactions  for  delegations  from  partner  countries,  enabling  their 
engagement  with  key  DPI  institutions  in  India,  such  as  the  Unique 
Identification  Authority  of  India  (UIDAI),  the  National  e-Governance 

3
Division (NeGD) of  MeitY , the National Payments Corporation of  India  
(NPCI) etc. These engagements enable partner countries to draw on  
India’s experience in developing their DPI and to discuss collaboration  
opportunities and implementation modalities for DPI solutions. Some of  
the recent visits include delegations from Sri Lanka, Kenya, Rwanda,  
Nepal, Indonesia, and South Africa. DPI-based projects funded by GoI are 
currently being implemented in Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Kenya, and Guyana;  
with DPI projects under finalisation with Mauritius and Seychelles.
(d & e) The roadmap for cooperation on DPI is developed in close  
consultation  with  the  respective  partner  countries,  as  India’s  
developmental  cooperation  model  is  demand  driven  and  as  per  the 
needs,  priorities  and aspirations  of  partner  countries. Finalisation of 
individual DPI solutions with partner countries is coordinated through  
technical  discussions  with  their  designated  authorities,  for  which 
representatives  of  concerned  Ministries  and  agencies  are  invited  to
