SHIPBUILDING AND SHIP REPAIR CLUSTERS IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
  
3292. SHRI APPALANAIDU KALISETTI: 
       
       Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पȅन, पोत पįरवहन और जलमागŊ मंũी 
 
  
(a) the details of shipbuilding and ship repair clusters approved across the country, 
including their locations, key features and funds allocated and released for their 
development; 
  
(b) the specific details of the shipbuilding and ship repair cluster approved in Andhra 
Pradesh, including the estimated investment, expected employment opportunities and 
key stakeholders involved; 
  
(c) the major upcoming investments aimed at enhancing container handling capacity 
and generating employment at ports in Andhra Pradesh;  
  
(d) the key shipbuilding and repair companies that have established or are planning to 
set up facilities within the shipbuilding and repair clusters in Andhra Pradesh; and 
  
(e) the current operational capacity of the shipbuilding and ship repair sector in Andhra 
Pradesh, key challenges being faced and the policy initiatives or incentives under 
consideration? 
  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a) to (b): Under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS), the Ministry of Ports, 
Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) has accorded in-principle approval for 
development of greenfield shipbuilding clusters at Dugarajapatnam in Andhra 
Pradesh, Kuchhadi in Gujarat and Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu, based on the 
applications submitted by the Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) formed between the 
respective State Government entities and the corresponding Major Port Authority 
under MoPSW. The details of the proposed clusters as per the preliminary Techno-

Economic Feasibility Report (TEFR) are at Annexure-1. At present no funds has been 
allocated or released for their development as DPRs for these projects are under 
preparation. 
The total indicative project cost for the shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam 
is ₹29,254 crore, as per the preliminary TEFR, comprising investment in the shipyard 
and port facilities, marine infrastructure, common infrastructure, land development, 
utilities and associated facilities.  
  The estimated investment and employment potential of all these proposed 
clusters is contingent upon finalization of detailed project report (DPR) by respective 
SPVs. The key stakeholders include SPV concerned and the prospective anchor 
shipyard. 
(c) As informed by the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh, development of a container terminal 
at Ramayapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh is a major upcoming investment envisaged 
for enhancing container handling capacity and to generate direct and indirect 
employment. 
  
(d) Government of Andhra Pradesh has entered into non-binding MoUs with Hindustan 
Shipyard Limited (HSL) and M/s J M Baxi Marine Services Private Limited for 
establishment of shipbuilding and ship repair facilities in the State.  
  
(e) As informed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, the current operational 
capacity of the shipbuilding and ship repair sector in Andhra Pradesh is concentrated 
at HSL in Visakhapatnam which features facilities such as a 80,000 deadweight 
tonnage (DWT) covered building dock, two slipways of 30,000 DWT capacity each 
and a 70,000 DWT dry dock. In addition, Kakinada has a number of private shipyards 
undertaking construction and repair of tugs, barges, fishing vessels, offshore support 
vessels and other small commercial vessels, catering primarily to the coastal and 
offshore sectors.  
  
The key challenges include high capital investment requirements, availability of 
contiguous waterfront land, development of common marine infrastructure, availability 
of skilled manpower and development of a supporting ancillary ecosystem. To address 
these challenges, the Government of Andhra Pradesh has notified the Andhra 
Pradesh Maritime Policy, 2024-29, under which shipbuilding and ship repair have been 
identified as focus sectors by providing incentives for eligible projects. Further 
shipbuilding and ship repair yards in Andhra Pradesh are also eligible to claim benefits 
under Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme, Maritime Development Fund and 
Shipbuilding Development Scheme of Government of India.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 07TH AUGUST, 2026
WORKING OF DOCTORS BEYOND WORKING HOURS
†3293. SHRI AJENDRA SINGH LODHI:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has sought a compliance report
from the Ministry of Health regarding the issue of postgraduate resident doctors being made
to work beyond the prescribed limits and the violation of the Postgraduate Medical Education
Regulations, 2023 at R.G. Kar Medical College, Kolkata;
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the action taken so far against the concerned officials
and the institution in the said matter and the details of the person held responsible for not
submitting the compliance report on time;
(c) whether resident doctors in various medical colleges are being made to work up to 80-100
hours per week which is a violation of the prescribed norms across the country, if so, the
details thereof, State/UT-wise; and
(d) whether the Government is ensuring strict compliance with the safety and working-hour
limits for resident doctors and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (d): Case No 441/90/0/2025 of National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was
referred to Ministry to submit the action taken report on a complaint dated 17.03.2025.
Matter was examined in the Ministry in consultation with National Medical Commission
(NMC) and submitted the report to NHRC, wherein it was informed as follows:
i. As per regulation 5.2 (ii) of the PGMER, 2023, "All post-graduate students will work
as full time resident doctors. They will work for reasonable working hours and will be
provided reasonable time for rest in a day”. Further, as per Regulation 9.1 of the
PGMER, 2023, "For non- compliance or omission, the PGMEB will penalize the
medical college/ institutions.". PGMEB, NMC is empowered to take action against

the concerned medical college/ institution, as per specified under Regulation 9.2 of
the PGMER, 2023.
ii. NMC Anti-Ragging Committee convened a meeting on 14.08.2024 to deliberate upon
the incident and its wider implications for the safety, well-being, and working
conditions of medical students and resident doctors across the country. As an
immediate measure, NMC issued an Advisory dated 13.08.2024 to all Medical
Colleges and Institutions.
iii. MoHFW/DGHS has issued directions to all Central Government Hospitals/Institutes,
AIIMSs and all Medical Colleges to ensure filing of institutional FIR within
maximum period of 6 hours of any incident of violence against doctors and other
healthcare personnel vide OM dated 16.08.2024 and also issued advisories to
States/UTs vide D.O. letters dated 23.08.2024 and 03.09.2024 to take immediate
measures for enhancing security and providing safer working environment for
medical professionals.
iv. The incident at R.G. Kar Medical College, West Bengal was taken up by the Hon’ble
Supreme Court of India in SMW (Crl) No. 2 of 2024, wherein the Hon'ble Court had
constituted a National Task Force (NTF) to formulate recommendations for redressal
of the issues regarding safety, well-being and working conditions of medical
professionals. The Report of NTF had been submitted to the Hon'ble Court in
November, 2024.
Also, as "Public Health and Hospitals" is a state subject, the respective State
Governments/UT Administrations prescribe norms for doctors' working hours, service
conditions, duty rosters in the concerned institutions, taking into account local requirements
and applicable service rules.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3294  
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
SAFETY AND SECURITY OF WOMEN THROUGH THE NIRBHAYA FUND  
  
3294. SHRI BUNTY VIVEK SAHU  
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether the Govemment  has taken effective measures for the safety and security of 
women through the Nirbhaya Fund, if so, the details thereof, including the benefits 
accrued to the State of Madhya Pradesh, particularly in Chhindwara district;  
(b)  whether the Govemment is considering the expansion of One Stop Centres, women's 
support services and other safety infrastructure to strengthen the safety and security of 
women in Chhindwara the said district, if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether the Govemment is implementation any special campaigns to further strengthen 
safety awareness and provide prompt assistance mechanisms for women and girls in 
rural and tribal areas, if so, the details thereof; and  
(d)  whether the Govemment is implementing any special action plan to ensure the effective 
and expeditious utilisation of the Nirbhaya Fund in the said State, if so, the details 
thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
   
(a) to (d): Aimed at enhancing the safety and security of women and girls in the country, 
Nirbhaya Fund has been set up as a dedicated non -lapsable corpus fund administered by the 
Department of Economic Affairs(DEA),Ministry of Finance in accordance with the framework 
and guidelines issued by the Government from time to time. The Institutional mechanism 
envisages a co -ordinated approach involving the concerned Central Ministries, State 
Governments and Implementing Agencies fo r conceptualization, execution and monitoring of 
the projects. Projects are conceptualized, planned and brought to the Inter - Ministerial 
Empowered Committee( EC) for appraisal and recommendation. Upon appraisal and 
recommendation of the proposals by the EC, the sponsoring Ministry’s   respective Competent 
Financial Authority (CFA)   gives the financial approval, after which the allocation of funds 
from the Nirbhaya Fund is made in the Budget of the sponsoring Ministry/ Department by the 
Ministry of Finance from the Nirbhaya Fund. The projects/ schemes under Nirbhaya Fund are 
demand driven and generally have staggered implementati on schedules and the responsibility 

of implementation of the project lies with the concerned sponsoring Ministries/Departments/ 
State Governments.  
The Inter Ministrerial  Empowered Committee also reviews the status of implementation of 
projects, and expenditure on approved projects from time to time in conjunction with the 
concerned sponsoring Ministries/ Departments/ State Governments/ UTs. The concerned 
Ministries / Depa rtments / State Governments/ UTs also monitor the progress of 
implementation at their own levels.  
Under the Nirbhaya Fund, upto the financial year 2025-26, a total amount of Rs. 320.71 Crore 
has been released/utilized for projects implemented through different implementing agencies 
in the State of Madhya Pradesh including the projects of Ministry of Women and Child 
Development viz. OSCs and WHL. 
One Stop Centre (OSC) provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one 
roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public spaces all 
across the country. It provides services like medical aid, legal aid an d advice, temporary 
shelter, police assistance and psycho -social counselling to needy women across the country. 
As on date, 991 One Stop Centres have been made operational across the country and since 
inception, i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026, ove r 15.20 lakh women have been assisted 
through One Stop Centres across the country. As on date, 63 OSCs are operational in Madhya 
Pradesh which have assisted over 1,65,475 women; out of which one OSC in Chhindwara is 
operational which has assisted 1095 women.  
Women Helpline (WHL -181) provides 24 -hour toll -free telecommunication services to 
support women in both emergency and non -emergency situations. It offers assistance to 
women affected by violence and provides information about government schemes and 
services. Since inception (1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026), over 1.04 crore women have 
been assisted through Women Helplines across the country. In the State of Madhya Pradesh, 
WHL has assisted over 3,83,834 women till 30th June, 2026.  
To strengthen convergence and ensure seamless access to support services, OSCs have been 
integrated with the Women Helpline (WHL), and so far, 661 OSCs have been integrated. 
Through this integration, women can be referred to appropriate services in a timel y and 
coordinated manner. Further, the Women Helpline has also been integrated with the 
Emergency Response Support System (ERSS -112), Child Helpline (1098) and other relevant 
service delivery mechanisms to facilitate prompt emergency response and effective  inter-
agency coordination. In addition, OSCs have also been integrated with Shakti Sadan to enable 
referral of women requiring long -term institutional support, rehabilitation and safe 
accommodation, thereby ensuring a continuum of care under the Mission S hakti framework. 
Details of projects and funds released/utilized out of Nirbhaya Fund for  the State of Madhya 
Pradesh are at Annexure.

CASE PENDENCY IN JUDICIARY 
 
†3295. SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV:  
SHRI SANJAY UTTAMRAO DESHMUKH: 
 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of cases currently pending in the Supreme Court, High Courts and subordinate 
courts across the country;  
(b) the details of the variation recorded in the number of pending cases during each of the last 
five years, State-wise;  
(c) the steps taken by the Government to ensure the speedy disposal of cases pending in the 
courts;  
(d) whether the Government maintains data on District-courts as well;  
(e) if so, the number of cases lying pending, particularly in district courts of Maharashtra, 
district-wise; and  
(f) the steps taken for the speedy disposal of the said pending cases? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) & (b): The details of number of cases currently pending in the Supreme Court, High Courts 
and Subordinate Courts across the country along with the number of pending cases during each 
of the last five years, State-wise, are at Annexure-I & II. 
 
(c) to (f): The data of all the cases pending in the courts across the country are available at 
National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG). The data of court cases pending in a district can be fetched 
from the NJDG. The number of cases pending, in the District Courts of Maharashtra, district-
wise, are at Annexure-III. 
 
Disposal of cases pending in various courts lies  within the domain of the judiciary. 
Timely disposal of cases in courts  depends on several factors which, inter -alia, include  
availability of adequate number of judges and judicial  officers, supporting court staff and 
physical infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, nature of evidence, co-operation of stake 
holders viz. bar, investigation agencies,  witnesses and litigants. However, the Government is 

2 
 
fully committed for speedy disposal of cases and reducing  pendency. The Government has 
taken several initiatives to  provide an ecosystem for faster disposal of cases by the  judiciary 
which, inter-alia, includes amalgamation of latest technologies for increasing access to justice 
and greater transparency under the e -Courts Mission Mode Project,  better infrastructure for 
courts, policy and legislative measures in the areas prone to excessive litigation, enactment of 
New Criminal Laws, establishment of Fast Track Special Courts, promoting Alternate Dispute 
Resolution mechanism and emphasis on human resource development.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3296  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
HEALTHY DIETS FOR CHILDREN  
 
3296. THIRU D M KATHIR ANAND:  
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  the details of the focus accorded to enhancing nutritional security for children through 
improved access to balanced diets, micronutrient -rich foods, protein supplementation 
and nutrition education under Government programmes;  
  
(b)  the details of the approach adopted for encouraging informed dietary choices among 
parents, caregivers and educational institutions by promoting awareness of healthy 
eating habits, quality food ingredients and age -appropriate nutrition for children; 
  
(c)  the details of the support extended for strengthening nutrition interventions through the 
Integrated Child Development Services, Poshan Abhiyaan/related schemes to States 
and Union Territories; 
  
(d)  the details of the collaboration with healthcare professionals, nutrition experts, 
educational institutions and food industry stakeholders for promoting scientific 
nutrition awareness; and 
  
(e)  the details of the measures being proposed for improving the availability, 
affordability/accessibility of nutritious foods to ensure better growth, health and 
cognitive development among children?  
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (e):     Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0)  has 
provisioned Supplementary Nutrition to all beneficiaries including Children (6 months to 6 
years), Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls (14-18 years). It is provided 
in the form of Take -Home Ration (THR), Morning Snacks and Hot Cooked Meal (HCM). 

Supplementary Nutrition is provided to the beneficiaries in accordance with the nutrition norms 
contained in Schedule -II of the National Food Security Act, 2013, revised in January 2023. 
The old norms were largely calorie -specific; however, the revised norms are more 
comprehensive and balanced in terms of both quantity and quality based on the principles of 
diet diversity that provides for quality protein, healthy fats and micronutrients ( Calcium, Zinc, 
Iron, Dietary Folate, Vitamin A, Vitamin -B6 and Vitamin B -12). Additional Nutrition is also 
provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children (6 months to 5 years) in the form of 
THR. 
The Ministry has recently issued the Comprehensive Guidelines for Supplementary Nutrition 
which emphasize on improving the quality, diversity and acceptability of Supplementary 
Nutrition, adherence to prescribed nutritional norms and quality standards. Gui delines also 
focus on nutrition and health education for caregivers, promoting the use and benefits of THR 
including counselling on age -appropriate complementary feeding practices and to conduct 
targeted awareness programmes focusing on reducing consumptio n of edible oils, salt and 
sugars in daily diets in line with the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024, released by the Indian 
Council of Medical Research – National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR -NIN). States and UTs 
are also advised to consult nutrition ex perts and technical institutes, like ICMR -NIN, 
Agricultural Universities, Home Science Colleges, etc., for formulating State -specific recipes 
for supplementary nutrition based on local palate/tastes using locally available foods.  
To improve acceptability and consumption of Supplementary Nutrition, States and UTs have 
been given full flexibility to design menus and recipes based on local food habits, cultural 
preferences and availability of indigenous ingredients. Supplementary nutr ition incorporates 
locally available cereals, millets, pulses, vegetables, nuts and other nutrient-rich foods, thereby 
promoting dietary diversity while ensuring greater acceptance among beneficiaries.  
One of the major activities undertaken under Mission Poshan 2.0 is Community Mobilization 
and Awareness Advocacy to educate people on nutritional aspects as adoption of good nutrition 
habit requires sustained efforts for behavioural change. State and UTs a re conducting and 
reporting regular sensitisation activities under Jan Andolans during Poshan Maah and Poshan 
Pakhwada, celebrated in the months of September and March -April, respectively. More than 
150 crore Jan Andolan activities have been conducted since 2018 through 16 Jan Andolans, 
each helped sensitizing not only the target beneficiaries but communities at large.  
Community Based Events (CBEs) have served as a significant strategy in changing nutritional 
practices and all Anganwadi workers (AWWs) are required to conduct two Community Based 
Events every month.  So far, around 10.5 crore CBEs have been reported on Poshan Tracker 
from April 2022 to June 2026. 
 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3297  
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
MALNUTRITION IN ANDHRA PRADESH  
3297. SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY:  
           DR. GUMMA THANUJA RANI:  
 
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether Government has conducted any assessment regarding malnutrition and 
anaemia among women and children in Andhra Pradesh, district -wise, particularly in 
tribal and rural districts, if so, the details thereof;  
  
(b)  whether the Government has reviewed utilisation gaps under Mission Saksham 
Anganwadi, if so, the details thereof; and  
  
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor?  
  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (c): A third-party evaluation and impact assessment of Poshan Abhiyaan was conducted 
by NITI Aayog in 2020 and it found the relevance of Poshan Abhiyaan to be satisfactory for 
tackling malnutrition in the country.    
In 2021, the World Bank conducted a survey under Poshan Abhiyaan across 11 States including 
Andhra Pradesh. The States were selected based on high prevalence of stunting among children 
and anaemia among women. The findings of the survey demonstrated improv ed nutrition 
behaviors with respect to the services delivered through the Poshan Abhiyaan. The survey also 
found that the program's nutrition messages reached more than 80% of women, and that 81% 
of women practiced exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months.  
An outcome-based evaluation study of Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission 
Poshan 2.0)  was conducted again by Development Monitoring and Evaluation 
Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog in 2025 in 12 States (including Andhra Pradesh) and one Union 
Territory. Evidence indicated that in its current form, Mission Poshan 2.0 represents the 
Government’s latest effort to holistically combat malnutrition and promote child development, 

by building on past programs with a converged and strengthened approach. High uptake and 
utilisation of Anganwadi services, such as supplementary nutrition, growth monitoring, and 
counselling, serves as a strong indicator that Poshan Abhiyaan has been frui tful in driving 
awareness and encouraging behavioural change among beneficiaries.  
Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD ) under Mission Poshan 2.0, has rolled 
out ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application as an ICT based governance tool for monitoring and 
reviewing of services being provided to beneficiaries. The application has enabled the Ministry 
as well as States & UTs to re view the implementation of the scheme on various parameters 
including health and nutrition status of the women and children and to make course corrections. 
For last mile tracking of Service Delivery, Facial Recognition System (FRS) in Poshan Tracker 
Application has been introduced for distribution of Take -Home Ration and to ensure that 
benefit is given only to the intended beneficiary registered in the application. Such Aadhaar 
based tracking has enabled proper identification of beneficiaries, prevention of  leakages and 
eliminating ghost entries.

MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF LEGAL AFFAIRS

ADVOCATES PROTECTION ACT 
  
3298. SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY: 
    
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has assessed the financial and professional challenges faced by 
young advocates during the initial years of legal practice, if so, the details thereof and if not, 
the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether the proposed Advocates Bill contains provisions for monthly stipends, skill 
development programmes, legal aid incentives, interest-free education loans, or other financial 
assistance for newly enrolled advocates, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to introduce a national policy for the welfare and social 
security of advocates, including mental health support and retirement benefits, if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether any timeline has been fixed for implementing these welfare measures after the 
enactment of the Bill; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor along with the steps being taken to 
improve the professional welfare and economic security of advocates in the country? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
  
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
  
(a) to  (e):  The Government is conscious of the financial and professional difficulties 
experienced by a substantial number of young advocates during the initial years of practice. In 
this regard, the Bar Council of India (BCI), a regulatory body for legal profession  under the 
Advocates Act, 1961 vide  Circular No. BCI:D:5383/2024 dated 15 October 2024, has 
recommended a minimum monthly stipend of Rs 20,000 for junior advocates working in urban 
areas and Rs 15,000 for junior advocates working in rural areas,  ordinarily for at least three 
years from the date of engagement.  There is no proposal under consideration regarding 
introducing a national policy for the welfare and social security of Advocates, including mental 

2 
 
health support and retirement benefits with the Government. The welfare of Advocates is 
governed by the Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 2001, under which the respective State Bar 
Councils administer the State Advocates' Welfare Funds and are empowered to extend financial 
assistance to Advocates in accordance with the provisions of the Act. Further, under the extant 
provisions as per Section 6(2) and Section 7(2) of the Advocates Act, 1961, the State Bar 
Councils and the Bar Council of India, respectively, are empowered to constitute one or more 
funds in the prescribed manner for providing financial assistance and implementing welfare 
schemes for indigent, disabled or other Advocates.

MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3299  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
ANGANWADI-CUM-CRECHES IN BIHAR  
  
 3299.  SHRI SUDAMA PRASAD:  
SMT. KANIMOZHI KARUNANIDHI:  
  
 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the number of Anganwadi -cum-Creches (AWCCs) and standalone Creches approved, 
currently operational along with the total number of Creche workers under the Palna  
Scheme under Mission Shakti, district-wise in Bihar and Tamil Nadu;  
(b)  whether Bihar has no functional Creches according to various reports, if so, the reasons 
therefor; 
(c)  whether the Government has observed low utilisation of Central funds released under 
the Palna Scheme in said States, if so, the details thereof; and  
(d)  the steps taken by the Government to ensure that all sanctioned Creches become 
operational within a time-bound manner in said States, if so, the details thereof?  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)   
  
(a) to (d):  The Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches (AWCCs) under Palna Scheme 
w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to 
children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers irrespective of their employment s tatus 
along with nutritional support, health and cognitive development of children, growth 
monitoring, immunization, education etc.   Palna component under Samarthya vertical of 
Mission Shakti is a centrally sponsored scheme and is implemented with a funding ratio of 
60:40 between Centre and State Governments and UTs with legislature except North East & 
Special Category States where ratio is 90:10. For UTs without legislature, 100% funding is 
provided by the Central Government.  Funds under the Scheme are released to the States/UTs 
in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Expenditure through the Single Nodal 
Agency (SNA)/SNA -SPARSH mechanism of the Public Financial Management System 
(PFMS).   
  
The State Government of Bihar has informed that 504 AWCCs are operational in the State and 
State Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that no A WCCs are operational in the State.

3300. Shri Ajay Kumar Mandal: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)    whether the ongoing war in the middle-east region has adversely affected the supply 
of fertilisers and fertiliser raw materials to the country as well as import costs and 
transportation; 
(b)    if so, the details of the quantity of urea DAP, MOP and other major fertilisers 
imported along with the availability and the increase/decrease recorded during the 
last five years and the current year, year-wise; 
(c)   whether the Government has taken any special steps to deal with the possible 
shortage of fertilisers through alternative sources of imports, long-term supply 
agreements and increase the domestic production, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)   whether the Government is working to ensure that the farmers of the country do not 
face any shortage of fertilisers during the crucial sowing and crop seasons, if so, the 
details thereof, State/district-wise including the Bhagalpur Parliamentary 
Constituency in Bihar? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) and (b) - The ongoing war in the middle-east region has disrupted global supply 
chains for fertilizers and raw materials, resulting in higher freight and insurance 
costs, shipment delays, and price volatility. However, fertilizer availability in the 
country remained largely adequate through diversified sourcing and Government 
interventions.

The details of the year wise availability of major fertilizers, from 2021-22 to 2025- 26 
as well as for Kharif 2026 (from 01.04.2026 to 03.08.2026) is placed at Annexure 
1.   
 
(c) and (d) -  Government has undertaken measures to diversify import sources by 
exploring procurement opportunities from various countries through engagement 
with Indian Missions abroad, aimed at strengthening the fertilizer supply chain and 
reducing vulnerabilities arising from global market disruptions. 
 
Moreover, the Government of India facilitates Indian fertilizer companies in entering 
into long term arrangements with overseas suppliers. In line with this, Indian 
companies have finalized agreements with Saudi Arabian and Russian companies 
for the annual supply of about 31 LMT and 26.50 LMT of DAP/ NPKs respectively 
to India in this year. For Muriate of Potash (MOP), Indian companies have finalized 
agreements for the supply of 4.80 LMT this year, sourced from Russia, Germany 
and Turkmenistan. 
 
The Government has taken the following steps to accelerate domestic production 
A. Urea: 
 
 With regard to Urea, the Government had announced New Investment Policy 
(NIP) – 2012 on 2nd January, 2013 and its amendment on 7th October, 2014 to 
facilitate fresh investment in the urea sector and to make India self-sufficient in 
the urea sector. Total 6 new urea units have been set up under NIP-2012 which 
includes 4 urea units set up through Joint Venture Companies (JVC) of 
nominated PSUs and 2 urea units set up by the private companies. The units set 
up through JVC are Ramagundam urea unit of Ramagundam Fertilizers and 
Chemicals Ltd (RFCL) in Telangana and 3 urea units namely Gorakhpur, Sindri 
and Barauni of Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL) in Uttar Pradesh, 
Jharkhand and Bihar, respectively. The units set up by private companies are 
Panagarh urea unit of Matix Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (Matix) in West 
Bengal; and Gadepan-III urea unit of Chambal Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. 
(CFCL) in Rajasthan. Each of these units has installed capacity of 12.7 Lakh 
Metric Tonne per annum (LMTPA). These units are highly energy efficient as 
they are based on latest technology. Therefore, these units have together added 
urea production capacity of 76.2 LMTPA, thereby total indigenous urea 
production capacity (Reassessed Capacity, RAC) has increased from 207.54 
LMTPA during 2014-15 to 269.42 LMTPA during 2026-27. Further, an exclusive 
policy for the revival of Talcher unit of FCIL through JVC of nominated PSUs 
namely Talcher Fertilizers Limited (TFL) by setting up a new Greenfield Urea 
plant of 12.7 LMTPA at coal gasification route has also been approved. Recently, 
the Union Cabinet has approved the proposal for setting up of a new Brownfield 
Ammonia-Urea Complex of 12.7 Lakh Metric Tonnes (LMT) annual capacity of 
Urea production within the existing premises of Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizer 
Corporation Limited (BVFCL), Namrup, Assam, named as Assam Valley 
Fertilizer and Chemical Company Ltd. (AVFCCL). These two projects are under 
execution phase. 
 

  
 
 
 
 The Government also notified the New Urea Policy (NUP) – 2015 on 25th May, 
2015 for the existing 25 gas-based urea units with one of the objectives of 
maximizing indigenous urea production beyond RAC.  The NUP-2015 has led to 
additional production of urea by 20-25 LMT as compared to the production during 
2014-15 annually. 
 Above steps together have facilitated increase of Urea production from level of 
225 LMT per annum during 2014-15 to a record Urea Production at 314.07 LMT 
during 2023-24. During 2025-26, 293.30 LMT of Urea was produced in the 
country. 
 In addition to this, on 15.07.2026, Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs 
(CCEA) approved National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 for Aatmanirbhar 
Bharat for making fresh investments in Urea Sector. 
B. P&K Fertilizers: 
 The Government has implemented the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme 
with effect from 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. 
Under the Scheme, P&K fertilizers are covered under Open General License 
(OGL), and companies are free to import or manufacture these fertilizers as per 
their business dynamics. 
 To reduce dependence on imported Phosphatic fertilizers and make country 
self-reliant measures have been taken to encourage domestic production 
through guidelines 18.01.2024 on reasonableness of MRP, wherein importers/ 
manufacturers and integrated manufacturers are given reasonable profit of 
8%/10% and 12% respectively.  
 Based on the requests, new manufacturing units or increase in manufacturing 
capacity of existing units have been recognized / taken on record under the NBS 
Scheme. 
 The number of P&K fertilizers covered under NBS Scheme has increased from 
22 grades in 2021 to 28 grades, as on date. 
 Freight Subsidy on SSP, which is an indigenously manufactured fertilizer, is 
being provided since Kharif, 2022 to promote SSP usage for providing 
Phosphatic or 'P' nutrient to the soil.  
 Further, the rates of nutrients under NBS scheme are decided on biannual basis 
to ensure availability of fertilizers under the Scheme. 
 
As a result of above efforts, highest ever domestic production of P&K fertilizers i.e. 
224.10 LMT has been recorded During 2025-26. 
 
Following Steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring timely and 
adequate supply of fertilizers in the country: 
 
i. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of 
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State 
Governments, assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of 
fertilizers. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of  
 

  
 
 
Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by 
issuing monthly supply plan and continuously monitors the availability. 
 
ii. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated 
Fertilizer Management System (iFMS). 
 
iii. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizer is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized 
well in advance to ensure timely availability. 
 
iv. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with 
manufacturers and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely 
placement of indents. 
 
v. Regularly coordinate with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, 
priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
vi. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
Accordingly, the availability of fertilizers, i.e. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKs, has 
remained adequate in the country during the last five years (FY 2021-22 to 2025-
26) and during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season (01.04.2026 to 03.08.2026). Details

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3302
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07th AUGUST 2026
GLOBAL TUBERCULOSIS REPORT 2024
3302. SHRI SUNIL BOSE:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the Global Tuberculosis Report 2024, which states that
India had the highest tuberculosis burden in the year 2023 contributing to 26 per cent of global TB
deaths, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the details of the allocation of funds for TB elimination in the country during each of the last
five years, year-wise and State/UT-wise;
(c) the initiatives taken by the Government to address the issue of multi drug-resistant TB in the
country; and
(d) whether the Government has been successful in the implementation of the National Strategic
Plan for Tuberculosis to eliminate TB by 2025, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons
therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)
(a) to (d) The Government has implemented National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)
under the aegis of National Health Mission (NHM). As per World Health Organisation’s
Global TB report 2024, it was estimated that India contributed to 26% of total TB deaths
globally in 2023, however as per Global TB Report 2025, the proportion reduced to 25%
in 2024.
With the implementation of the National Strategic Plan for TB, as per the World Health
Organization’s Global TB Report 2025 the country’s estimated TB incidence (per lakh
population) has declined by 21% from 237 in year 2015 to 187 in year 2024, almost twice the
global decline (12%). Estimated TB mortality (per lakh population) declined by 25% from 28
in year 2015 to 21 in year 2024. The treatment coverage increased from 53% in 2015 to 92%
in 2024, which led to reduction in missing cases from 15 lakhs to less than 1 lakh.
Measures taken by the Government to address multi drug-resistant TB across the country are
as under:
 Early detection through intensified screening in OPD/IPD and community based active
case finding campaign with focus on vulnerable population and congregate settings
 Provision of free drugs and diagnostics to TB patients including for drug-resistant TB

 Universal Drug Susceptibility Testing (UDST) for all TB patients to detect drug-resistant
TB through 11,296 Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) laboratories at district & sub
-district levels
 Established a network of 108 Line Probe Assay, 74 Liquid Culture Testing Laboratories,
37 Intermediate Reference Laboratories and 6 National Reference Laboratories for
diagnosis of drug resistance and quality assurance
 For decentralized treatment, 815 Drug Resistant TB treatment centres are established
 Introduction of shorter, safer, all oral drug-resistant TB treatment regimen, which includes
BPaLM regimen (Bedaquiline, Pretomanid, Linezolid and Moxifloxacin) for management
of drug- resistant TB cases
 Intensified Information, Education & Communication (IEC) campaigns to reduce stigma,
enhance community awareness and improve health seeking behaviour
 Track & monitor notified TB cases through Ni-kshay portal
Under NHM, funds for NTEP are provided as part of RCH Flexipool to all State/UTs. Further,
the details of allocation of funds for TB elimination in the country during last five years, year-
wise and State/UT-wise, is placed as Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3303 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
 
Establishment of Fertilizer Manufacturing Units in Amritsar 
 
3303. Shri Gurjeet Singh Aujla: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Union Government is considering to support fertilizer unit in Amritsar to 
reduce import dependency, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether it is true that such a unit would not only reduce transportation costs and import 
dependency, but also generate massive employment opportunities for local youth, support 
agriculture and reduce the burden of excessive subsidy by enabling cheaper domestic 
production, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) whether the proposal of such units under the schemes promoting self-reliance in agri- 
inputs and prioritise border areas like Amritsar for such strategic investment, if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
 (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (c): With regard to Urea, the Government had announced New Investment Policy (NIP) 
– 2012 on 2nd January, 2013 and its amendment on 7th October, 2014 to facilitate fresh 
investment in the urea sector and to make India self-sufficient in the urea sector. Total 6 new 
urea units have been set up under NIP-2012 which includes 4 urea units set up through Joint 
Venture Companies (JVC) of nominated PSUs and 2 urea units set up by the private 
companies. The units set up through JVC are Ramagundam urea unit of Ramagundam 
Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd (RFCL) in Telangana and 3 urea units namely Gorakhpur, 
Sindri and Barauni of Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL) in Uttar Pradesh, 
Jharkhand and Bihar, respectively. The units set up by private companies are Panagarh urea 
unit of Matix Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (Matix) in West Bengal; and Gadepan-III urea 
unit of Chambal Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (CFCL) in Rajasthan. Each of these units has 
installed capacity of 12.7 Lakh Metric Tonne per annum (LMTPA). These units are highly 
energy efficient as they are based on latest technology. Therefore, these units have together 
added urea production capacity of 76.2 LMTPA, thereby total indigenous urea production 
capacity (Reassessed Capacity, RAC) has increased from 207.54 LMTPA during 2014-15 to 
269.42 LMTPA during 2026-27. Further, an exclusive policy for the revival of Talcher unit of  
 
 

-2- 
 
FCIL through JVC of nominated PSUs namely Talcher Fertilizers Limited (TFL) by setting up 
a new Greenfield Urea plant of 12.7 LMTPA at coal gasification route has also been 
approved. Also, setting up of a new Brownfield Ammonia-Urea Complex named as Assam 
Valley Fertilizer and Chemical Company Ltd. (AVFCCL) with an annual capacity of 12.7 Lakh 
Metric Tonne of Urea through Joint Venture within the existing premises of Brahmaputra 
Valley Fertilizer Corporation Limited (BVFCL), Assam has been approved. These two 
projects are under execution phase. 
 
Also, the Government notified the New Urea Policy (NUP) – 2015 on 25th May, 2015 for 
the existing 25 gas-based urea units with one of the objectives of maximizing indigenous 
urea production beyond RAC.  The NUP-2015 has led to additional production of urea by 
20-25 LMT as compared to the production during 2014-15 annually.  
 
Above steps together have facilitated increase of Urea production from level of 225 LMT 
per annum during 2014-15 to a record Urea Production at 314.07 LMT during 2023-24. 
During 2025-26, 293.30 LMT of Urea was produced in the country. 
 
In addition to this, on 15.07.2026, CCEA approved National Investment Policy for Urea-
2026 for Aatmanirbhar Bharat (NIPU-2026) for making fresh investments in Urea Sector. 
 
For P&K Fertilizers, the Government has implemented Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) 
Scheme w.e.f. 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. Under the Scheme, 
P&K fertilizers are covered under Open General License (OGL) revival, expansion and 
modernisation of manufacturing units and companies are free to import/ manufacture these 
fertilizers as per their business dynamics. 
  
To reduce dependence on imported Phosphatic fertilizers and make country self-
reliant   measures have been taken to encourage domestic production through guidelines 
18.01.2024 on reasonableness of MRP , wherein importers/ manufacturers and integrated 
manufacturers are given reasonable profit of 8%/10% and 12% respectively; based on the 
requests, the new manufacturing units or increase in manufacturing capacity of existing units 
have been recognized / taken on record under the NBS Scheme; the number of P&K 
fertilizers covered under NBS Scheme has increased from 22 grades in 2021 to 28 
grades; Freight Subsidy on SSP, which is an indigenously manufactured fertilizer, is being 
provided since Kharif, 2022 to promote SSP usage for providing Phosphatic or 'P' nutrient 
to the soil. Further the rates of nutrients under NBS scheme are decided on biannual basis 
to ensure availability of fertilizers under the Scheme. 
 
To reduce the country's dependence on imports of fertilizer raw materials, the 
Government, under the Mode-2A of Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition 
(SIGHT) scheme of National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM), MNRE, a provision has 
been made for procurement of approx. 7 LMT per annum of Green Ammonia for a period of 
10 years by the Fertilizer companies for production of P&K fertilizers. Towards 
operationalization of this initiative, Green Ammonia Purchase Agreements (GAPA) between 
Green Ammonia Producers and Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI), and 
Green Ammonia Sales Agreements (GASA) between Fertilizer Companies and SECI, were 
signed on 30.03.2026. 
 
However, at present there is no proposal for setting up or extending support to a urea 
fertilizer manufacturing unit in Amritsar is under consideration of the Government.

3304. SHRI MALVINDER SINGH KANG:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any scheme to establish Government Medical
Colleges in all districts of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise;
(c) whether Rupnagar (Ropar) district in Punjab has been considered under the said scheme;
and

construction of the Medical College in the district?

THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE

Scheme (CSS) for ‘Establishment of new medical colleges attached with existing
district/referral hospitals’ with preference to underserved areas and aspirational districts,

up of Medical College at Rupnagar (Ropar) has been received from the State of Punjab.

 Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a)  the details of the funds released/utilised under POSHAN Abhiyaan since FY 2020 -21; 
  
(b)  the details of the anganwadi centres equipped with functional devices for real -time

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT

Scheme for Adolescent Girls (of 14 -18 years age in Aspirational Districts and North -Eastern 
region) have been subsumed under the umbrella Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Posha n 2.0

implementation of various activities lies with the States and UTs.

Mission Poshan 2.0 empowers the frontline functionaries by providing them with smartphones. 
All Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) are provided with internet connectivity charges. 
Additionally, there is a provision of a set of 4 Growth Monitoring Devices (GMDs) 
(Infantometer and Stadiometer for length and height measurement, Weighing Scale -Infant and 
Weighing Scale -Mother & Child for weight measurement) at all Anganwadi Centres (AWC) 
in the country for regular growth measurement of all registered beneficiaries. Further, data 
entry on Poshan Tracker application of all indicators including growth measure ment is done 
by the Anganwadi Workers using smartphones. Additionally, a 2% buffer for smartphones and 
5% buffer for GMDs has been provisioned to be kept and maintained at the district level so 
that input is not adversely affected because of malfunctioning /non-availability of these items. 
As per guidelines, smartphones and GMDs beyond 4 years are eligible for replacement.  
Data of malnutrition indicators is collected under National Family Health Survey (NFHS) by 
the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Various rounds of the NFHS since 1992 -93 have 
shown improvement over the years in malnutrition indicators across India. De tails of these

Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD) under the Mission has rolled out 
‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application as an ICT based governance tool for monitoring and 
tracking of all beneficiaries on various indicators. The State -wise data of nutrition i ndicators 
among children under five years in the country is available at the Poshan Tracker public 
dashboard: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics.  
Various measures have been taken by the MoWCD to improve nutritional outcomes including 
in low performing States are placed below:  
• Supplementary Nutrition in the form of Hot cooked meal (HCM) and Take -Home 
Ration (THR) is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), Pregnant Women, 
Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the nutrition norms 
contained in Schedule-II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. Additional Nutrition 
is also provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children in form of Take -
Home Ration (THR). 
• One of the major activities undertaken under Mission Poshan 2.0 is Community 
Mobilization and Awareness Advocacy to educate people on nutritional aspects as 
adoption of good nutrition habit requires sustained efforts for behavioural change. State 
and UTs a re conducting and reporting regular sensitisation activities under Jan 

Andolans during Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada celebrated in the months of 
September and March -April, respectively. More than 150 crore Jan Andolan activities 
have been conducted since 2018 through 16 Jan Andolans, each helped sensitizing not 
only the target beneficiaries but communities at large.  
• Community Based Events (CBEs) have served as a significant strategy in changing 
nutritional practices and all Anganwadi workers (AWWs) are required to conduct two 
Community Based Events every month.  So far, around 10.5 crore CBEs have been 
reported on Poshan Tracker from April 2022 to June 2026.  
• MoWCD and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW) have jointly released 
the Protocol for Management of Malnutrition in Children to prevent and treat severely 
acute malnutrition in children and for reducing associated morbidity and mortality.  
• Under the Mission, two lakh Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) have been approved to be 
upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis for delivery of improved nutrition and for ECCE 
activities. These Saksham Anganwadis are equipped with better infrastructure such as 
LED screens, w ater filtration system, Poshan Vatika, Early Childhood Care and 
Education (ECCE) material and Building as Learning Aid (BaLA) paintings.  
• Ministry of Tribal Affairs has launched Dharti Aaba Janjati Gram Unnat Abhiyan 
(DAJGUA) aimed at improving the socio-economic condition of tribal communities by 
adopting saturation coverage of tribal families in tribal majority areas and aspirational 
block ST villages. Under DAGJUA, 875 AWCs have been sanctioned for construction.  
• Under PM -JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan) being 
implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) which aims to provide basic 
facilities such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, 
health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified 
households a nd sustainable livelihood opportunities in convergence with 9 -line 
Ministries including MoWCD. A total of 2,500 Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) have been 
sanctioned for construction in PVTG (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups) areas.  
• In convergence with the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee 
Scheme (MGNREGS) of Ministry of Rural Development, construction of AWCs is 
facilitated. Further, States and UTs have also been advised to continue to tap funds for 
construction of A WC buildings from various schemes such as Member of Parliament 
Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS), Rural Infrastructure Development Fund 
(RIDF), Finance Commission Grants to Panchayati Raj Institutions, Multi -Sectoral 
Development Programme (MSDP) of Mi nistry of Minority Affairs, etc.  
• MoHFW organises Village Health Sanitation and Nutrition Days (VHSNDs) for 
provision of maternal and child health services and creating awareness on maternal and 
child-care including nutrition in convergence with MoWCD.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE 
                                                            
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3307 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 07th AUGUST, 2026 
 
SANCTIONED STRENGTH OF JUDGES IN HIGH COURTS 
 
3307. PROF. SOUGATA RAY: 
           
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the growing pendency of cases in various High 
Courts despite periodic increase in the sanctioned strength of Judges, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to substantially increase the sanctioned strength of 
Judges in all High Courts, on the lines of the recent increase in the sanctioned strength of Judges 
of the Supreme Court;  
(c) if so, the details thereof including the proposed increase and the timeline for 
implementation, High Court-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the additional number of Judges 
required in each High Court based on pendency, institution and disposal of cases, judge -to-
population ratio and regional requirements, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the measures being taken by the Government in consultation with the judiciary to ensure 
timely filling of vacancies, strengthening of judicial infrastructure and reduction of pendency 
in the High Courts? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW  
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to ( e): The Judges of the High Courts are appointed under Article 217 and 224 of the 
Constitution of India and according to the procedure laid down in the Memorandum of 
Procedure (MoP) prepared in 1998 pursuant to the Supreme Court Judgment of October 6, 
1993 (Second Judges case) read with their Advisory Opinion of October 28, 1998 (Third Judges 
case).  
 

2 
 
As per the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP), the responsibility for initiation of 
proposals for appointment of Judges in the Supreme Court vests with the Chief Justice of India, 
while the responsibility for initiation of proposals for appointment of Judges in the High Courts 
vests with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court, in consultation with two senior-most 
puisne Judges of the High Court. As per the MoP, the High Courts are required to make 
recommendations at least 06 months before the occurrence o f a vacancy. However, this time 
limit is rarely observed. For appointments to the High Courts, the views of concerned State 
Government are obtained in accordance with the MoP. The recommendations also have to be 
considered in the light of such other reports as may be available to the Government in respect 
of the names under consideration. The recommendations of the High Court Collegium, the 
State Governments and the Government of India are then forwarded to the Supreme Court 
Collegium (SCC) for advice. Appo intment of Judges in the higher judiciary is a continuous, 
integrated and collaborative process between the executive and the judiciary. It requires 
consultation and approval from various Constitutional Authorities both at State and Central 
level. Only those persons whose names have been recommended by the SCC are appointed as 
Judges of the High Courts.  
 
 The Judge strength of the High Courts is increased from time to time. The strength of 
High Courts has increased from 906 in 2014 to 1122 Judges in 2026. 
 
Disposal of cases pending in various courts lies within the domain of the judiciary . 
Timely disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter -alia, include 
availability of adequate number of judges and judicial officers, supporting court staff and 
physical infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, nature of evidence, co-operation of stake 
holders viz. bar, investigation agencies, witnesses and litigants. However, the Government is 
fully committed for speedy disposal of cases and reducing pendency. The Government has 
taken several initiatives to provide an ecosystem for  faster disposal of cases by the judiciary 
which, inter-alia, includes amalgamation of latest technologies for increasing access to justice 
and greater transparency under the e -Courts Mission Mode Project, better infrastructure for 
courts, increase in strength of subordinate judiciary, policy and legislative measures in the areas 
prone to excessive litigation,  enactment of New Criminal Laws, promoting Alternate Dispute 
Resolution mechanism and emphasis on human resource development.

Fertilizer Subsidy in Kerala 
3308. Shri Kodikunnil Suresh: 
 Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of fertilizer subsidy released along with the quantity of subsidised 
fertilizers made available in Kerala since 2019-20, fertilizer-wise and year-wise;  
 
(b) whether the Union Government has received any representations from the 
Government of Kerala regarding shortage, delayed supply/inadequate allocation of 
subsidised fertilizers, if so, the details thereof and the action taken thereon;  
 
(c) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding the impact of rising 
international fertilizer prices and import costs on the availability and timely supply of 
subsidised fertilizers in the said State, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(d) the quantity of urea, DAP, MOP, NPK and other subsidised fertilizers supplied to 
the said State during the last five years, district-wise; and  
 
(e) the steps taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to ensure adequate, 
timely and affordable availability of subsidised fertilizers to farmers in the said State, 
particularly paddy, coconut, rubber, spice and horticultural growers? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (e): Under the DBT in Fertilizers system, 100% subsidy on various fertilizer 
grades is released to fertilizer companies based on the actual sales made to 
beneficiaries. The subsidy is disbursed after Aadhaar authentication of the 
beneficiaries through PoS devices installed at each retail shop. Accordingly, fertilizers 
are supplied to all farmers at subsidized rates on a no-denial basis. Since funds are 
not allocated or disbursed in a district-wise or State-wise basis, such data is not 
maintained.  The details of the total amount of fertilizer subsidy disbursed by the

The recent geopolitical tensions disrupted global supply chains for fertilizers and 
raw materials, resulting in higher freight and insurance costs, shipment delays, and price 
volatility. However, fertilizer availability in the country remained largely adequate through 
diversified sourcing and Government interventions. Government has undertaken measures to 
diversify import sources by exploring procurement opportunities from various countries. 
Moreover, the fertilizer industry has also collectively procured fertilizers and raw materials 
through an industry consortium to ensure transparent price discovery, improve bargaining 
power with global suppliers, and secure timely availability of fertilizers and raw materials. The 
budgetary allocation for fertilizer subsidy is reviewed periodically, based on which, the process 
for seeking additional budgetary allocation, on requirement, is undertaken, as per the extant 
provision. 
 
The following Steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring timely and 
adequate supply of fertilizers across the States/UTs, including the State of Kerala: 
I. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, assesses the State-wise & 
month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, 
Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing 
monthly supply plan and continuously monitors the availability. 
II. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the country by an 
online web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS). 
III. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other fertilizer is met 
through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in advance to ensure timely 
availability.  
IV. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers and 
importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
V. Regularly coordinate with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient rakes, priority to 
fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
VI. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the concerned State 
government. 
Accordingly, the availability of fertilizers i.e. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has remained 
adequate in the State of Kerala since 2019-20 (i.e. in FYs 2019-20 to 2025-26). The information 
regarding requirement, availability and sales of these fertilizers in the State during the said 
period is placed at Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3309  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
NUTRITIONAL STATUS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN  
3309. SHRI ZIA UR REHMAN: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the nutritional status of children and pregnant 
women under POSHAN Abhiyaan, if so, the details thereof;  
(b)  the details of malnutrition cases reported during the last three years, State -wise; and 
(c)  the details of the corrective measures being taken to improve nutrition and strengthen 
Anganwadi services? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) to (c):  Under the Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0), 
the ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application has been rolled out by Ministry of Women and Child 
Development (MoWCD ) as an ICT based governance tool for continuous monitoring and 
tracking of all services being provided to the beneficiaries registered at Anganwadi Centres 
(AWCs). Technology under Poshan Tracker is being leveraged for dynamic identification of 
stunting, wasting, under -weight prevalence among children under 5 years of age group. The 
State-wise and year -wise information on nutrition indicators among children under 5 years is 
available at Poshan Tracker dashboard: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics.  
Various measures have been taken by the MoWCD to improve nutritional outcomes and 
strengthen Anganwadi services:  
• Under Mission Poshan 2.0, two lakh Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) located in 
Government buildings have been approved to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis for 
delivery of improved nutrition and for ECCE activities. These Saksham Anganwadis  
are equipped with better infrastructure such as LED screens, water filtration system, 
Poshan Vatika, Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) material and Building as 
Learning Aid (BaLA) paintings. 
  

• Supplementary Nutrition in the form of Hot cooked meal (HCM) and Take -Home 
Ration (THR) is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), Pregnant Women, 
Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the nutrition norms 
contained in Schedule-II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. Additional Nutrition 
is also provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children in form of Take -
Home Ration (THR). 
• MoWCD and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have jointly released the Protocol 
for Management of Malnutrition in Children to prevent and treat severely acute 
malnutrition in children and for reducing associated morbidity and mortality.  
• Mission Poshan 2.0 empowers the frontline functionaries by providing them with 
smartphones along with data recharge facility. Further, there is a provision of Growth 
Monitoring Devices (GMDs) as Infantometer, Stadiometer, Weighing Scale-Infant and 
Weighing Scale -Mother & Child at each Anganwadi Centre (AWC) for the regular 
growth monitoring of registered beneficiaries.  
• Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) conduct structured home visits to support pregnant 
women, lactating mothers, and young children (0 -3 years) through nutrition 
counselling, caregiving guidance, and promotion of early childhood development.  
• One of the major activities undertaken is Community Mobilization and Awareness 
Advocacy in the form of Jan Andolans (Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada celebrated 
in the months of September and March -April respectively) to educate people on 
nutritional aspects as adoption of good nutrition habit requires sustained efforts for 
behavioural change. 
• Poshan Vatikas are set up under Mission Poshan 2.0 at Anganwadi Centers across the 
country to encourage consumption of local and seasonal fruits, vegetables, thereby 
improving diet-diversity and increase the intake of micronutrients.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
 
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026 
 
EVACUATION OF SEAFARERS 
 
 3310. SHRI TANUJ PUNIA: 
 
        Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state: 
पƣन, पोत पǐरवहन और जलमाग[ मंğी 
 
(a) the names of the Ministers and Embassies with whom coordination 
mechanisms have been established for rapid medical response and emergency 
evacuation under the Seafarer First Plan; 
(b) whether the Government has made it mandatory for shipowners and 
recruitment agencies not to force any Indian seafarer to undertake duty on sensitive 
routes without adequate protection; and 
(c) the role of dedicated liaison officers to be appointed to assist the families of 
affected sailors?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
  
(a) The Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways is coordinating through Ministry of 
External Affairs and Indian Embassies all over the world and also  through Directorate 
General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) a subordinate body under this Ministry 
with Port State Authorities, Flag State Authorities and Recruitment and Placement 
Service License [RPSL] agencies, for rapid medical response and emergency 
evacuation under the seafarer First Plan.  
(b)  The Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), has issued a 
series of advisories in view of the maritime security environment, in conflict-affected 
regions, including the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, Black Sea, and the Yemen/Red 
Sea region. These advisories are precautionary in nature and are intended to enhance 
the safety and security of Indian seafarers. The details are placed at Annexure. 
(c)  The Government, through the Directorate General of Maritime Administration 
(DGMA), has designated dedicated officers for continuous coordination, 
communication, and welfare support to Indian seafarers and their families during 
maritime emergencies and crisis situations. These officers function as liaison officers 
and are responsible for maintaining regular engagement with the Next of Kin (NoK), 

Recruitment and Placement Service Licence (RPSL) agencies, shipping companies, 
Indian Missions abroad, maritime administrations, and other concerned stakeholders 
to ensure timely assistance and coordinated response. Vide Order dated 02.03.2026, 
a dedicated 24×7 Quick Response Team has been constituted in DGMA to provide 
immediate response, evacuation coordination, crisis management, and welfare 
support. The responsibilities assigned to the designated officers include: 
 Maintaining continuous communication with the families and Next of Kin (NoK) 
of affected seafarers. 
 Coordinating with RPSL agencies, shipping companies, Indian Missions 
abroad, port authorities, and other stakeholders for obtaining real-time 
information and facilitating timely assistance. 
 Providing immediate support through the DG Communication Centre operating 
round-the-clock via dedicated telephone, WhatsApp, and email channels. 
 Facilitating evacuation, repatriation, welfare assistance, and dissemination of 
advisories issued by the Directorate General of Maritime Administration and the 
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. 
 Monitoring the status and location of affected seafarers, submitting periodic 
situation reports, and ensuring prompt response to emergencies affecting the 
safety, security, and welfare of Indian seafarers.  
Accordingly, a structured mechanism has been established through designated liaison 
officers and a dedicated 24×7 response team to ensure continuous engagement with 
affected families and timely coordination for all welfare, relief, communication, and 
support-related matters.  
  

ANNEXURE 
  
Advisories to Ensure the Safety and Security of Indian Seafarers: 
Following advisories operate alongside the standing maritime security architecture 
established under DGS Circular No. 08 of 2024 dated 10.04.2024 and are supported 
by a 24-hour Control Room, continuous real-time monitoring through the DG 
Communication Centre under DGMA, and the issue of a Situation Report every 24 
hours. 
i. DGS Advisory (14.01.2026) – Advisory to Indian Seafarers and Shipping 
Stakeholders in view of MEA Advisory on Iran, advising shipping companies not 
to deploy Indian seafarers to Iran until further orders, requiring close monitoring 
of Indian crews in the region, and directing seafarers to follow advisories issued 
by the Embassy of India and the Ministry of External Affairs. 
ii. DGS Circular 09 of 2026 (28.02.2026) – Urgent Advisory to Indian Seafarers 
and Shipping Stakeholders in view of Escalating Situation in Iran, requiring 
Indian seafarers in Iran to remain vigilant, register with the Embassy of India, 
coordinate for safe departure where feasible, and directing stakeholders to 
immediately provide details of Indian seafarers in affected areas. 
iii. DGS Circular 10 of 2026 (06.03.2026) – Safety Advisory for Indian Seafarers 
and Shipping Stakeholders Operating in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and 
Adjacent Waters, advising continuous vigilance, compliance with ISPS Code 
security measures, establishment of 24x7 emergency contact mechanisms, 
liaison with Indian Missions, emergency preparedness, and psychological 
counselling support for seafarers and their families where necessary. 
iv. DGS Circular 11 of 2026 (07.03.2026) – Social Media Advisory to Maritime 
Stakeholders and Seafarer Community, directing maritime stakeholders to 
refrain from circulating unverified information, rumors, fake videos or 
speculative reports and to rely only on authenticated information from official 
sources. 
v. DGS Circular 21 of 2026 (07.04.2026) – Safety Advisory for Indian Seafarers 
Ashore in Iranian Ports and Onboard Vessels Operating in or Around Iranian 
Waters, advising seafarers in Iran to remain at designated locations, avoid 
unnecessary travel, maintain heightened vigilance, follow Embassy advisories 
and remain in contact with company representatives, while also providing 24×7 
emergency assistance contact details. 
vi. DGS Circular 31 of 2026 (13.06.2026) – Precautionary Measures for Indian 
Seafarers in view of the Heightened Security Situation in the Gulf Region, 
reiterating heightened security vigilance, directing shipping companies and 
RPSL companies to restrict deployment of Indian seafarers to conflict areas 
until further orders (except emergency crew changes with consent), monitoring 
and reporting requirements, and dissemination of verified security information. 
vii. DGS Circular No. 36 of 2026 {15.07.2026) : In view of renewed attacks on 
merchant vessels, DGS Circular No. 36 of 2026 mandated the implementation 
of full International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code security 

measures and advised against the deployment of Indian seafarers on voyages 
transiting through the gulf region. 
viii. DGMA Circular No.41 of 2026 (23.07.2026) – Advisory issued for Indian and 
foreign flagged vessels carrying Indian seafarers operating in the Black Sea, 
requiring enhanced caution, voyage specific security assessments, strict 
adherence to security advisories and immediate reporting of incidents. 
ix. DGS Circular No.42 of 2026 (23.07.2026) - Advisory issued for vessels 
operating in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, Southern Red and adjoining Yemen 
waters, directing shipowners and masters to exercise utmost caution, 
continuous monitor security, developments and implement additional risk 
mitigation measures.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3311 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
Warangal Rake Point 
 
3311.   Shri Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy: 
                Shri Eatala Rajender: 
            
 Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the rake point remained non-operational for fertilizer handling at 
Warangal in the State of Telangana for Rabi Season 2025-26, if so, the details thereof 
and the reasons therefor; 
 
(b) whether it is true that the said rake point caters to the fertilizer requirements of 
six districts of the erstwhile Warangal region, accounting for approximately twelve per 
cent of the Rabi cropped area of the said State, if so, the details thereof, district-wise; 
 
(c) whether it is a fact that although Chintalpally in the said State has been notified 
as the new rake point and an iFMS code has been created, operations have not yet 
commenced, if so, the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) whether alternative arrangements are insufficient to meet this scale of demand 
immediately, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) whether the State Government of Telangana requested Union Government to 
permit fertilizer operations at the said district rake point, to avoid any inconvenience to 
the farmers, if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (e)  As per the information received from Ministry of Railways, Warangal Goods 
shed (WL) has been kept under restriction for handling bagged consignment from 

27.10.2025, due to safety reasons. However, Chintalapally (CLE) goods shed at 
12.3 km from Warangal has been notified for handling bagged consignment and 
operational since 10-09-2025. A total of 83 rakes of fertilizers during the FY 2025-
26 and 74 fertilizer rakes during the FY 2026-27 (upto July 2026) have been handled 
here. Further, alternate arrangements made at Chintalapally (CLE) Goods Shed are 
sufficient enough to handle the inward traffic of Warangal (WL). Due to availability 
of full length line at Chintalapally, the unloading time has been reduced by avoiding 
split placement. Being away from busy city area, it is avoiding pollution and road 
congestion in Warangal. Hence, more number of rakes can be dealt at Chintalapally. 
Besides, State Government of Telangana has informed that fertilizer operations 
have commenced through Chintalpally with effect from November-2025. 
Further, State Government of Telangana has informed that the Warangal Rake 
Point used to cater to the requirement of erstwhile Warangal District. The details are
