GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS  
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3312 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
Excessive Use of Fertilizers 
 
3312.  Dr. Prabha Mallikarjun: 
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding nitrate contamination 
of groundwater, pesticide residues and environmental impacts associated with 
excessive fertilizer usage, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any studies has been conducted regarding the impact of fertilizer and 
agrochemical use on human health, water quality and ecosystem sustainability during 
the last five years, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has identified regions affected by groundwater contamination 
and soil degradation linked to agricultural chemical use, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the measures being taken to promote sustainable fertilizer practices, nano-fertilizers, 
bio-fertilizers and environmentally responsible nutrient management; and 
(e) whether any groundwater quality monitoring, soil restoration/sustainable agriculture 
initiatives have been implemented in Karnataka, particularly in Davanagere district, if 
so, the details thereof, district-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
 (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
 
(a) to (c)   The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) informed that they generate 
groundwater quality data at the regional scale through its groundwater quality monitoring 
programme and various scientific studies. Groundwater quality is monitored across the 
country through the Ground Water Quality Monitoring Stations, and the analyzed data are 
published in the Annual Ground Water Quality Reports of CGWB. As per the Annual 
Ground Water Quality Report–2025, 20.71% of groundwater samples analyzed were found 
to contain nitrate above the permissible limit of 45 mg/L (BIS IS 10500). Nitrate 
contamination above the permissible limit has been observed in parts of 502 districts 
across 26 States/UTs. The State/UT-wise details are placed at Annexure-I. Further, 
CGWB informed that they have not conducted any specific studies on pesticide residues, 

environmental impacts of excessive fertilizer usage, health impacts of fertilizer/ 
agrochemical use, or soil degradation specifically linked to agricultural chemical use. 
Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka informed that they have not 
conducted any exclusive study on nitrate contamination of groundwater, pesticide residues 
and environmental impacts associated with excessive fertilizer usage. However, balanced 
application of NPK fertilizers in conjunction with organic manure (FYM/bio-fertilizers) to 
maintain soil health, organic carbon content and crop productivity is being promoted. 
Imbalanced and excessive use of nitrogenous fertilizers (especially Urea) leads to soil 
acidity/alkalinity, secondary and micronutrient deficiencies (such as Zinc and Boron) and 
secondary leaching of nitrates into shallow aquifers. Further, ICAR and the Directorate of 
Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage (DPPQ&S) under the Monitoring of Pesticide 
Residues at National Level (MPRNL) scheme regularly analyse the  samples of  food 
commodities and surface water sources. Pesticide residue levels exceeding Maximum 
Residue Limits (MRL) remain under control. Under the MPRNL project and the State Sector 
Program, samples of fruits, vegetables, grains, fish/marine products, herbs, and water are 
drawn to test for pesticide residues. If samples are found to contain residues exceeding 
the Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) or traces of off-label pesticide usage, farmers in the 
concerned areas are sensitized about the ill effects of excessive and off-label chemical 
applications. 
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) informed that long-term studies 
conducted by them have shown that imbalanced nutrient application, particularly sole 
application of nitrogen, leads to decline in crop yield and soil health. Excess nitrogen is 
primarily lost through nitrate leaching, resulting in groundwater nitrate contamination, with 
Nitrate concentrations exceeding the permissible limit of 10 mg/L in some areas. Studies 
also showed that groundwater nitrate levels increase with fertilizer application rates, with 
higher contamination observed in high fertilizer-use areas. 
(d)   Government of India is promoting sustainable and balanced use of fertilizers through 
judicious use of synthetic fertilizers, adopting alternate fertilizers, promoting organic/natural 
farming and implementing resource conservation technologies. Achieving balanced 
fertilization requires a multi-pronged strategy that integrates policy, technology, and farmer 
participation. The following measures have been adopted for balanced use of fertilizers: 
(i) Integrated Nutrient Management (INM): It enables the efficient, economical, and 
sustainable application of nutrients by judiciously integrating organic inputs, mineral 
fertilizers, and biological sources. INM recognises that neither chemical fertilizers nor 
organic inputs alone are sufficient to meet the complete nutritional requirements of crops. 
It also promotes crop rotation and residue management that enhance system diversity, 
disrupt pest and disease cycles, and improve nutrient use efficiency. 
(ii) Soil Health & Fertility Scheme: Government promotes judicious use of fertilizer 
through Soil Health & Fertility scheme since 2014-15. Under the scheme Soil Health Cards 
(SHCs) is provided to farmers, to promote balanced and integrated nutrient management 

for improving productivity and soil fertility. Soil samples are processed as per standard 
procedures and analyzed for parameters such as pH, Electrical Conductivity, Organic 
Carbon, available Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Sulphur, and micronutrients (Zinc, 
Copper, Iron, Manganese & Boron). The diagnostic soil health assessment of farmer fields 
is taken up periodically so as to issue SHCs at least once in 3 years. Since 2014-15 as on 
date, 25.90 crore Soil Health Cards have been generated/ distributed. Total of 8313 Soil 
Testing Labs have been established across the country. Soil Test-Based Fertilizer 
Recommendations is a fundamental and essential step in balanced fertilization. Based on 
test results, soils are classified as low, medium, or high in nutrient content. Fertilizer doses 
are increased for nutrient-deficient soils and reduced where nutrient levels are already 
sufficient. The Soil Health Card Scheme supports this approach by providing farmers with 
field-specific soil data, enabling them to apply fertilizers more accurately and avoid 
excessive use. 
(iii) National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF): NMNF was approved by the Union 
Cabinet on 25.11.2024 as a standalone Centrally Sponsored Scheme to promote Natural 
Farming. Natural Farming (NF) is a chemical free farming, involving livestock (preferably 
local breed of cow) integrated natural farming methods and diversified crop systems rooted 
in the Indian traditional knowledge. The mission aims to promote nature-based sustainable 
systems of farming with on farm inputs thus reducing dependency on chemical inputs, 
improve soil health, and reduction in input cost. Budget outlay approved for NMNF is 
₹2481.00 crore (GoI share: ₹1584.00 crore and States’ share: ₹897.00 ). So far, 18,825 
clusters have been formed, 19.00 lakh farmers have been registered, 9.00 lakh hectares 
area has been covered and 6,388 Bio-Input Resource Centres (BRCs) established. The 
Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) –Online Certification System has been initiated for 
the certification of natural agricultural products. Till date more than 14.00 lakh farmers have 
been registered with more than 6 lakh certificates issued. 
(iv) Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY): Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana of 
RKVY is being implemented since 2015-16 in all States/UTs except North Eastern States 
for promoting organic farming. The scheme stresses on end-to-end support to farmers 
engaged in organic farming i.e. from production to processing, certification and marketing. 
Primary focus of the schemes is to form organic clusters, with preference to small and 
marginal farmers, to create a supply chain. Till date, 18.84 lakh hectares area has been 
covered and 33.94 lakh farmers benefited from the scheme. A total of ₹2608.72 crore 
(central share) has been released under PKVY Scheme to States/UTs. 
(v) Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region 
(MOVCDNER): MOVCDNER is being implemented since 2015-16 to promote organic 
farming in the North Eastern States. MOVCDNER is a centrally sponsored scheme with 
100% GoI share. The scheme focuses on enhancing farmers participation in agriculture 
value chain through promotion of organic farming and development of Farmer Producer 
Organisations (FPOs). Till date, 2.36 lakh hectares brought under organic farming and 2.70 
lakh farmers benefited. 427 Unique FPOs and 52 extended FPOs (Total-479 FPOs) have 

been formed under MOVDCDNER. 933 infrastructure such as storage, processing units 
etc. have been created. All 8 north east states have developed their own organic product 
brands through the support of the scheme. Till date an amount of ₹1491.14 crore (central 
share) has been released. 
(vi) PM-PRANAM (PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness, Nourishment and 
Amelioration of Mother Earth) Scheme: PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness 
Generation, Nourishment, and Amelioration of Mother-Earth (PM-PRANAM) is an initiative 
which aims to support the mass movement initiated by States and Union Territories (UTs) 
to preserve the health of Mother Earth through the promotion of sustainable and balanced 
fertilizer use, adoption of alternative fertilizers, promotion of organic farming, and 
implementation of resource conservation technologies. All States/UTs are covered under 
the PM-PRANAM scheme. Under the PM-PRANAM scheme, there is a provision to provide 
incentives to States/UTs for reduction of consumption of chemical fertilizers (Urea, DAP, 
NPK, MOP) in a given financial year, compared to the average consumption over the 
previous three years, equivalent to 50% of the fertilizer subsidy saved. 
 
(vii) Promotion of Nano Fertilizers : Nano Fertilizers are plant nutrients packaged in tiny 
particles called nanomaterials, allowing nutrients to be released slowly and absorbed by 
crops more efficiently, with minimal waste. In order to promote the use of Nano Fertilizers 
among farmers across the country, the following measures have been undertaken by the 
Government: 
 
 Use of Nano Fertilizers is promoted through different activities such as awareness 
camps, webinars, field demonstrations, Kisan Sammelans and films in regional 
languages etc. 
 Nano Fertilizers, like Nano Urea and Nano DAP, are made available at Pradhan 
Mantri Kisan Samridhi Kendras (PMKSKs) by concerned companies. 
 For ease in application and utilization of Nano fertilizers, like Nano Urea and Nano 
DAP, through foliar application, initiatives such as innovative spraying options like 
'Kisan Drones' and distribution of battery operated sprayers at retail points are 
undertaken. For this purpose, pilot training and custom hiring spraying services 
through Village Level Entrepreneurs are actively promoted.  
 
(viii) Market Development Assistance (MDA): To promote production of soil carbon 
enhancers namely Fermented Organic Manure (FOM), Liquid FOM (LFOM), and Phosphate 
Rich Organic Manure (PROM), Department of Fertilizers provides assistance of Rs. 
1500/MT to Compressed Biogas (CBG) operators under Central Sector GOBAR-dhan 
(Galvanized Organic Bio Agro Resources-Dhan) scheme. 
 
(ix)   Promotional efforts by ICAR : ICAR promotes soil test-based balanced and 
Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) through the combined use of organic and inorganic 

nutrient sources. The Council has developed Soil Test Crop Response (STCR)-based 
district general fertilizer recommendations, site-specific nutrient management tools, crop- 
and soil-specific biofertilizers, including phosphorus-solubilizing microorganisms and liquid 
biofertilizers, besides technologies for organic manures, biomineral fertilizers and 
Fermented Organic Manure (FOM). ICAR also promotes slow and controlled-release 
fertilizers, band placement of fertilizers, efficient irrigation and fertigation practices, and has 
developed organic farming packages for 80 cropping systems under its Natural Farming 
Network Programme. These technologies are disseminated through frontline 
demonstrations, farmer training and awareness programmes. 
Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka informed that following 
measures being taken in the State: 
(i) Balanced use of Fertilizers is being recommended based on soil test reports and 
also through promotion of adoption of Nano Urea and Nano DAP, Fermented 
Organic Manure (FOM), Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM), green manure 
crops and biofertilizers for which extensive awareness campaigns are being 
conducted through newspapers, handouts, training programmes, and other publicity 
initiatives in collaboration with IFFCO and other fertilizer manufacturing companies. 
As of now, a total of 10,85,560 bottles of Nano Urea and 4,77,610 bottles of Nano 
DAP have been sold across the State. Extensive awareness campaigns are being 
conducted under the 'Khet Bachao Andolan' and other departmental schemes 
to educate farmers about the harmful effects of excessive use of urea and other 
chemical fertilizers. The campaigns promote balanced and judicious fertilizer 
application. Use of Bio-fertilizers helps to fix nitrogen and to dissolve/mobilize 
nutrients naturally. 
(ii) Promoting sustainable agricultural practices such as crop rotation and agroforestry 
to mitigate soil degradation. Plant cover crops between seasons to trap nutrients 
and reduce soil erosion. Use of Green manure seeds is being promoted to increase 
the organic carbon content, to improve the physical, chemical and biological 
activities of the soil. 
(iii) Promoting precision farming. 
(iv) Natural farming / organic farming is being promoted in 1,272 clusters Under National 
Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) by providing incentives to the farmers. 
 
(e)  The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) informed that they monitor groundwater 
quality across the country including Karnataka state and its Davanagere district through its 
Ground Water Quality Monitoring Stations. As per the Annual Ground Water Quality 
Report, 2025, the district-wise and parameter-wise number and percentage of groundwater 
samples exceeding the permissible limits in the State of Karnataka including Davanagere 
district is placed at Annexure II. In Davanagere district, out of 19 groundwater samples 
analyzed, 7 samples (36.8%) exceeded the permissible limit for nitrate, 2 samples 

(10.53%) exceeded the permissible limit for fluoride, while none exceeded the permissible 
limit for electrical conductivity.      
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) informed that they have undertaken 
high-resolution (1:10,000 scale) Land Resource Inventory (LRI) in several districts of 
Karnataka, including Davanagere, through ICAR-National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land 
Use Planning (NBSS&LUP). The LRI provides detailed information on soils, land capability, 
erosion, drainage and land suitability, and supports soil restoration, sustainable land use 
planning, watershed development, crop diversification, site-specific nutrient management 
and climate-resilient agriculture, enabling efficient management of land and water 
resources. 
Department of Agriculture, Government of Karnataka informed that during 2026–27, 
under various State sector and Central Sector schemes organic inputs viz green manure 
seeds, organic fertilizers, bio-fertilizers, micronutrients and soil amendments are being 
distributed to farmers through Raitha Samparka Kendras at subsidized rates as an initiative 
towards sustainable agriculture. District wise target details are at Annexure III. Soil 
restoration & sustainable agriculture initiatives initiated in Davanagere district are as 
mentioned below: 
(i) Vasudhamrutha Scheme: A flagship initiative to increase organic carbon levels 
and to improve physical, chemical, and biological properties of soil. An amount of 
Rs. 14.78 Lakhs earmarked for distribution of Green manure seeds at 75% subsidy.  
(ii) Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme: Customized nutrient recommendations are 
delivered to farmers to prevent over-fertilization and rectify site-specific deficiencies 
by analysing for 12 parameters. During last five years 51,380 soil health cards have 
been distributed to farmers.  
(iii) Integrated Nutrient Management (INM): Micro-nutrients, bio-fertilizers (such as 
Azotobacter and Rhizobium), and soil amendments (e.g., gypsum and lime for 
acidic/alkaline soils) through Raitha Samparka Kendra’s (RSKs) are being 
distributed through various schemes of department.  
(iv) National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF): Natural Farming practices are 
being promoted in 48 clusters covering in 2400 Ha.  
Further, Governemnt of Karnataka informed that to minimize top soil run-off and 
recharge groundwater levels, soil and water conservation structures such as check dams, 
trench-cum-bunds, nala bunds, and contour bunding are being promoted through 
Watershed Development Programmes (Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) 
and Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY)).

SET UP OF MEDICAL COLLEGES IN ODISHA
†3313. SHRI RUDRA NARAYANPANY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the policy of the Government to set up medical colleges in each district of the
country is still in effect and if so, the details thereof;
(b) the total number of districts in which medical colleges and hospitals are functioning at
present;
(c) whether the Government provides any incentives to medical colleges and hospital set up
by the State Governments;
(d) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise particularly in Odisha; and
(e) whether the State Government of Odisha proposes to provide any special package to
medical colleges and hospitals to be opened in Dhenkanal and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (e): The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare administers a Centrally Sponsored
Scheme (CSS) for ‘Establishment of new medical colleges attached with existing
district/referral hospitals’ with preference to underserved areas and aspirational districts,
where there is no existing Government or private medical college. The fund sharing
mechanism between the Centre and State Governments is in the ratio of 90:10 for North
Eastern and Special Category States, and 60:40 for others. Under the Scheme, all the
envisaged 157 Government Medical Colleges have been approved in the country including
seven (07) medical colleges (Balasore, Baripada (Mayurbhanj), Bolangir, Koraput, Puri in
Phase-I, Jajpur in Phase-II & Kalahandi in Phase-III) in Odisha. Of these, 139 medical

Further, Government Medical College (GMC) at Dhenkanal, Odisha is a State
funded project.

INCIDENCE OF GESTATIONALDIABETES MELLITUS
3314. SHRI ESWARASAMYK:
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the rising incidence of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
(GDM) among pregnant women in India as indicated by recent clinical studies and
national health surveys, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the prevalence data on GDM reported during the last five years, year-wise and State-wise;
(c) whether the Government has taken note of the significant variation between NFHS survey
findings and hospital-based clinical estimates indicating possible under-diagnosis of
GDM in the country, if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken by the Government under the National Health Mission (NHM),
RMNCH+A framework and other maternal health programmes to ensure universal
screening, early diagnosis and effective management of GDM at the primary healthcare
level?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (c) The details of the ICMR-INDIAB National Study (ICMR-INDIAB-24)
conducted on Prevalence of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in India is available in the
following link:
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12744553/
(d) Under National Health Mission (NHM), the Government of India has taken various
initiatives/steps to ensure universal screening, early diagnosis and effective management
of GDM at the primary healthcare level, which placed as below;
 The Government of India has released Guidelines on Diagnosis and Management of
Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) in pregnant women in 2014 and revised Guidelines
in 2018.
 Financial assistance is provided to States/UTs for ensuring the availability of logistics
for GDM screening and for capacity-building of frontline healthcare providers, including

Medical Officers, Staff Nurses, Community Health Officers (CHOs), Auxiliary Nurse
Midwives (ANMs), and Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs).
 Universal screening for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) through the Oral
Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) has been incorporated into the essential antenatal care
(ANC) package for all pregnant women.
 Pregnant women identified as GDM are tracked till 45th day of delivery under
Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA/Extended-PMSMA). Further,
incentives are provided to ASHA and High Risk Pregnant (HRP) women for 3 additional
follow-ups visit.
 Implementation and progress of GDM screening are monitored through supportive
field visits and periodic National and State level review meetings.
 Universal GDM screening is promoted through regular Information, Education and
Communication (IEC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) activities to
enhance awareness and encourage early detection and timely management.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 3316 
ANSWERED ON- 07/08/2026 
 
MANUFACTURING OF AYUSH DRUGS 
 
3316. SHRI NA VEEN JINDAL 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: - 
(a) the total number of complaints received by the Government regarding false, misleading or 
unfounded advertisements issued by AYUSH drug manufacturers during each of the last three 
years; 
(b) the action taken against the erring companies in this regard; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to strengthen the regulatory/advisory framework to 
curb such advertisements; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHA V) 
(a) & (b) The Ministry of Ayush has been implementing the Pharmacovigilance Programme for 
Ayush drugs since 2018 to monitor the safety of Ayush medicines through surveillance, 
reporting and assessment of suspected adverse drug reactions, thereby promoting their safe and 
rational use. The Programme also monitors misleading advertisements relating to Ayush drugs 
to curb false and exaggerated claims and safeguard consumer interests. The Programme was 
incorporated under the Ayush Oushadhi Gunavatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardh an Yojana 
(AOGUSY) in 2021. The total number of complaints received by the Ministry regarding 
misleading advertisements related to Ayush drugs under Pharmacovigilance Program for Ayush 
drugs in last three years are attached at Annexure-1.  
Further, Ministry of Ayush has launched an IT enabled online portal “Ayush Suraksha” to track 
the reported Misleading Advertisements (MLAs)/Objectionable Advertisements (OAs) and 
Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) in 2025.  As per information received from State/UTs, the 
misleading advertisements reported on Ayush Suraksha Portal since its inception and action 
taken thereon are attached at Annexure-2. 
(c) & (d) As per the section 8 of Drugs & Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) 
Act, 1954, States and UTs are empowered to notify officers to enforce the provisions of Drugs 

& Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954  and Rules there under . It 
encompasses the provisions for prohibition of misleading advertisements and exaggerated 
claims of drugs and medicinal substances including Ayush medicines, which appear in the print 
and electronic media and Ministry of Ayush has issued advisories and gives direction to SLAs 
to enforce and regulate as per the provision of this Act. 
 
Further, the f ollowing actions have been taken by the Ministry to strengthen the 
regulatory/advisory framework to curb misleading/objectionable advertisements- 
 
i. Pharmacovigilance Program for Ayush drugs under  Ayush Oushadhi Gunavatta evam 
Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) is working through a three -tier network of a 
National Pharmacovigilance Centre (NPvCC), Five Intermediary Pharmacovigilance 
Centres (IPvCs) and 97 Peripheral Pharmacovigilance Centres (PPvCs) established across 
the country. To enhance public awareness regarding Ayush medicines and its objectionable 
advertisements, a total of 4,165 awareness programmes for Ayush professionals and Public 
have been conducted, benefiting 3,71,477 participants by Pharmacovigilance centres. 
ii. Ministry of Ayush has launched an IT enabled online portal “Ayush Suraksha” to track the 
reported Misleading Advertisements (MLAs)/Objectionable Advertisements (OAs) and 
Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) in 2025. 
iii. Ministry of Ayush issued a public notice  on 08.10.2024  & 24.08.2025, informing the 
general public about the facts regarding Ayush drugs/medicines and urging them to avoid 
patronizing misleading advertisements, which was published in 100 leading newspapers 
across India in Hindi, English, and several regional languages. 
iv. Further Central Government has notified the Coordinator, National Pharmacovigilance 
Coordination Centre, All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi, under Information 
Technology Act, 2000 as the nodal officer for the purpose of issuing notice to intermediaries 
in relation to any information, data or communication link residing in or connected to a 
computer resource controlled by the intermediary being used to commit the unlawful act, 
in respect to the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954, the 
National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020 and the National 
Commission for Homeopathy Act, 2020. 
v. Circulars and advisories with the objective of curbing the dissemination of false, 
misleading, or unsubstantiated information regarding Homoeopathy have been issued by 
The Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy (BERH), National Commission for 
Homoeopathy.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
LOK SABHA 
UN-STARRED QUESTION No. 3317  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
SAMBAL AND SAMARTHYA COMPONENTS UNDER MISSION SHAKTI  
3317. SHRI MALAIYARASAN D:  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state : 
(a)  the current status of implementation of Mission Shakti, including the projects/services 
operational under its Sambal and Samarthya components in Tamil Nadu;  
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised for implementation of the said Mission 
in the said State during the last five years;  
(c)  the number of beneficiaries provided assistance through One Stop Centres, Women 
Helpline services and other women empowerment initiatives under the said Mission, 
district-wise including Kallakurichi Parliamentary Constituency;  
(d)  whether the Government has assessed the challenges faced in implementation of said 
Mission, including availability of trained personnel, infrastructure gaps and awareness 
among women, particularly in rural and remote areas of the State; and  
(e)  if so, the details of the steps being taken by the Government to enhance access to 
protection, rehabilitation, skill development and livelihood opportunities for women 
through this Mission in the said State?  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
  
(a) To (e) The Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes in the country for the welfare of women and children, which are placed 
under three verticals, viz. (1) Mission Shakti, for safety, protection and empowerment  of 
women; (2) Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 for improving nutrition & health indicators in 
the country; and (3) Mission Vatsalya, for protection and welfare of children in difficult 
circumstances.  

The ‘Mission Shakti’ aims at strengthening interventions for women safety, security and 
empowerment. Mission Shakti comprises of two verticals ‘Sambal’ for safety and security of 
women and ‘Samarthya’ for empowerment of women.  
The ‘Sambal’ has components of One Stop Centre (OSC), Women Helpline (WHL), Beti 
Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) and Nari Adalat.  
1. One Stop Centre (OSC)  provides integrated and immediate support and assistance 
under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and 
public spaces all across the country. It provides services like medical aid, legal aid and 
advice, temporary s helter, police assistance and psycho -social counselling to needy 
women across the country. As on date, 991 One Stop Centres have been made 
operational across the country and since inception, i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 
2026, over 15.20 lakh women ha ve been assisted through One Stop Centres across the 
country. As on date, 59 OSCs are operational in the State of Tamil Nadu; out of which 
one OSC is operational in Kallakurichi district and two OSCs are operational in Salem 
district, which have assisted o ver 1,82,957 women. 
2. Women Helpline (WHL -181) provides 24 -hour toll-free telecommunication services 
to support women in both emergency and non-emergency situations. It offers assistance 
to women affected by violence and provides information about government schemes 
and services. Since inception (1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026), over 1.04 crore 
women have been assisted through Women Helplines across the country. In the State 
of Tamil Nadu, WHL has assisted over 2,59,509 women till 30th June, 2026.  
3. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao  helps to address Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues 
of empowerment of girls and women. The scheme tries to create mindset and 
behavioural changes towards the girl child by informing, influencing, motivating, 
engaging, and empowering various stakehol ders. BBBP has transformed from a policy 
initiative into a national movement by mobilizing various stakeholders, including 
government agencies, media, civil society, and the public at large.  As per latest reports 
of Health Management Information System (HM IS) of Ministry of Health & Family 
welfare (MoHFW), the Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) is showing improving trends and has 
increased from 918 to 929 at national level during 2014-15 to 2025-26 (provisional). In 
the State of Tamil Nadu, the Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) has increased from 917 to 937 
during 2014-15 to 2025-26 (provisional). 
As per UDISE data of Ministry of Education, Gross enrolment ratio of girls in the 
schools at secondary level has increased from 75.51% in 2014-15 to 83.4% in 2025-26. 
In the State of Tamil Nadu, the Gross enrolment ratio of girls in the schools at secondary 
level has increased from 93.82% in 2014 -15 to 99.6% in 2025-26. 
4. Nari Adalat scheme provides a platform for alternative grievance redressal for women 
at the gram panchayat level. The Adalats are mandated to help women in distress at the 
panchayat level in resolving smaller issues relating to domestic violence, and other 
gender-based violence by negotiation, mediation, and reconciliation with mutual 
consent for accessible justice. 
The scheme is demand driven and piloted in 50 Gram Panchayats each in the State of 
Assam and the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir in FY 2023 -24. In the State of 
Bihar, Jharkhand, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, 
Punjab, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Tripura and Uttar Pradesh, Nari Adalat is operational in 

10 Gram Panchayats in each State. In FY 2025-26, 10 Gram Panchayats each in 4 States 
of Goa, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttarakhand and 5 Gram Panchayats each in the UTs of 
Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu and Andaman & Nicobar Islands has also 
been approved for operationalization of Nari Adalat.  
The ‘Samarthya’ has components of Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, Pradhan Mantri Matru 
Vandana Yojana (PMMVY), Palna and SANKALP: Hub for Empowerment of Women 
(SANKALP: HEW).  
1. Shakti Sadan: Under the overarching ‘Mission Shakti’, erstwhile schemes of ‘Swadhar 
Greh’ – Home for women in difficult circumstances and ‘Ujjawala ’- Home for women 
rescued from Trafficking, have been merged w.e.f. 01.04.2022 and are now known as 
‘Shakti Sadan Scheme’, which is an Integrated Relief and Rehabilitation Home for 
women in distressful situations including trafficked women.   It aims at creating a safe 
and enabling environment for women in such difficult situations, to enable them to 
overcome the adverse circumstances. Shakti Sadan is helpful towards support for 
women in distress, providing shelter and rehabilitation support including those affected 
of trafficking.  
Under the Scheme, financial assistance is provided for running of Shakti Sadan in 
rented premises. At present, 46 Shakti Sadans are functional in the State of Tamil Nadu 
benefiting around 2050 beneficiaries. There are 02 Shakti Sadans operational in 
Kallakurichi district of Tamil Nadu. 
2. Sakhi Niwas: Sakhi Niwas Scheme (Working Women Hostel) under the overarching 
Mission Shakti, aims to promote availability of safe and conveniently located 
accommodation for working women in urban, semi-urban and also in rural areas where 
employment opportunity for wom en exists and women undergoing job -related 
training.  Provision of a Day Care Centre for the children of residents is an important 
component of the Scheme. At present, 59 Sakhi Niwas are operational in Tamil Nadu, 
benefiting around 3,341 women.   
3. Palna: The Ministry introduced Palna Scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day 
care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 
years) of all mothers irrespective of their employment status along with nutritional 
support, health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring, 
immunization, education etc. State Government of Tamil Nadu has intimated that 
Standalone creches were operational till March, 2025 and AWCCs are not operational 
under Palna Scheme. 
4. PMMVY: The Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) w.e.f. 01.01.2017 across 35 States and UTs 
in the country including Tamil Nadu (excluding Telangana, which is under process of 
onboarding on the PMMVY portal). PMMVY is a Centrally Sponsored Maternity 
Benefit Scheme under which cash incentives of ₹5,000/ - is provided directly to the 
Bank/ Post Office account of the beneficiary in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode 
for first child. The eligible beneficiar ies receive the remaining cash incentive, as per 
approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana after 
institutional delivery, so that on an average a woman gets ₹6,000/ -. Cash incentive of 
₹6,000/- is also provided under PMMVY to eli gible beneficiaries for second child 
subject to the second child being a girl.  

Benefits amounting to Rs. 1,135.63 crores have been extended to approximately 22.23 
lakh women in the State of Tamil Nadu through this scheme since inception of the 
scheme (01.01.2017) till 31.07.2026. The details of the beneficiaries paid under the 
PMMVY Scheme in the State of Tamil Nadu during the last 5 Financial years is as 
below:

2. 2022-23 1,35,752

*Due to ongoing process at States and UTs level in implementation of APIs related to PMMVY 
onboarding on SNA -SPARSH system, the beneficiary payment data (for FY 2025 -26) is only 
an estimate based on data from PFMS portal  
  
The district-wise details of the beneficiaries paid under the PMMVY Scheme during the last 5 
Financial Years in the State of Tamil Nadu (including Kallakurichi and Salem districts of the 
Kallakurichi Parliamentary Constituency) is at Annexure-I. 
5. SANKALP: HEW: The SANKALP: HEW (Hub for Empowerment of Women) 
functions as a Project Monitoring Unit (PMU) for all components of Mission Shakti. It 
serves as a single window system to bridge the information and knowledge gap 
regarding schemes and facilities available for women as well as guide them to avail the 
benefits and entitlements. 
As on date, total 35 State SANKALP: HEWs and 742 District SANKALP: HEWs are 
functional, including one District Hub for Empowerment of Women (DHEW) each in 
the Kallakurichi and Salem districts of the Kallakurichi Parliamentary Constituency. 
Further, 2,14,145 women have been assisted in the State of Tamil Nadu since FY 2024-
25.   
Mission Shakti is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme and implementation of this scheme lies with 
the State Governments and UT Administrations. Funds are being released on the basis of 
guidelines of Department of Expenditure, prescribed for Single Nodal agency (S NA) or SNA 
SPARSH of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). The details of funds released/ 
expenditure in the State of Tamil Nadu during the last five years under Mission Shakti is at 
Annexure-II. 
Once in a year, the Programme Approval Board (PAB) monitors with States and UTs, the 
progress of activities under the scheme and reviews status of achievement of objectives and 
effective delivery of services to women and children. Apart from this, official s of the Ministry 
continuously review the scheme through meetings, video conferencing and by making field 
visits to States and UTs from time to time. Further, to strengthen digital monitoring, the 
Ministry has developed the Mission Shakti Dashboard for rea l-time monitoring and effective 
implementation of the Scheme. The Dashboard facilitates monitoring of beneficiaries assisted, 
services provided, infrastructure, activities and facilities at the District, State and National 
levels.  

Two third party evaluations of the schemes of the Ministry, including the Mission Shakti 
Umbrella Scheme have been conducted in 2020 and again in 2025 through NITI Aayog. The 
studies have found the relevance, effectiveness and sustainability of the scheme as satisfactory. 
The Ministry has also undertaken measures to strengthen the capacity of Women Helpline and 
One Stop Centre functionaries through regular training, technical support and continuous 
handholding of States/UTs. Capacity building programmes have been organised with the 
support of NIMHANS, SPNIWCD and C -DAC, covering areas such as psycho -social 
counselling, gender sensitisation, ethical call management, case management, dashboard 
operations, referral mechanisms and convergence with various stakeholders. C -DAC als o 
provides regional and hands-on training, technical support, dashboard support, troubleshooting 
and MIS/data analytics support to States/UTs.  
Several steps have been undertaken by the Government of India to strengthen the 
implementation and awareness of the PMMVY scheme across the country. Some of these are 
as under: 
i. New portal for PMMVY, which is completely paperless was launched in March 2023. 
As per earlier Guideline, physical forms were required to be filled and uploaded in the 
earlier PMMVY-CAS portal for onward process. In new system, physical application 
forms have been eliminated and complete online solution has been given.  
ii. Payments are through Adhaar Bridge Payment System [ABPS] as PMMVY portal is 
enabled for Aadhar -based biometric verification (by means of facial recognition) to 
confirm identity details of the applicants.  
iii. All the mandatory provisions like Aadhaar verification, DBT enablement of bank 
account etc. are checked at the time of registration for faster processing.  
iv. Search and Track Status for all enrolled beneficiaries to check the approval and 
payment status of their applications.  
v. Grievance Lodging and status module for all citizens to lodge any PMMVY related 
grievance. The Module directly sends the grievance to the implementing authorities 
thus saving time and leads to swifter resolution.  
vi. PMMVY toll-free and multi lingual helpline (1515) is available for PMMVY related 
enquiries and grievances. For transparency purposes, the Applicants/ beneficiaries 
receive SMS in one of the 12 languages at different stages such as registration of 
application, rejection of registration, payment etc.  
vii. PMMVY Portal is LGD compliant till AWC level. LGD Seeding is introduced up to 
State/District/Block/ Village/GP/Ward level.  
viii. Open API allows the freedom to share data with other Central and State 
Ministry/Department. 
ix. MIS Data can be generated at State/ District/ Block/ Village/ Ward/ Project/ Sector/ 
Anganwadi level for detailed monitoring/ analysis.  
x. PMMVY will be used by Anganwadi/ ASHA workers for data centric operations and 
viewing reports. 
xi. Available database of the PW&LM from Poshan Tracker is used to create a “Due List” 
of potential beneficiaries on PMMVY Portal accessible at AWW/ASHA level.  
Additionally, the Ministry of Women & Child Development conducts various awareness 
programs including those on Maternity Benefits through SANKALP: HEW scheme for all 
States and UTs. It includes various Information, Education and Communication (IEC) and 
Behavior Change Communication (BCC) activities such as Prabhat Pheri, Nukkad Natak, 

Newspaper Advertisements, Airing Radio Jingles, Selfie Campaign, Door to Door Campaign, 
Community Programmes which are conducted at field functionary levels. Further, the Ministry 
also runs special campaign for registration of eligible beneficiaries in all  the States and UTs 
under PMMVY on a periodic basis.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3318
TO BE ANSWERED ON 07TH AUGUST, 2026
STRENGTHENING OF PRIMARY HEALTH SERVICES IN REMOTE AREAS
†3318. SHRI CHINTAMANI MAHARAJ:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a significant increase in the number of beneficiaries, treatments
and hospital admissions under the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
(AB-PMJAY) in Chhattisgarh, including Surguja district and if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether special steps have been taken by the Union Government to strengthen primary
healthcare services, screening, diagnostic services and health insurance coverage through
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) in tribal and remote regions of the State, such as
Surguja District and if so, the details thereof;
(c) the progress made under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and other digital
health initiatives to expand and integrate digital health services across various health schemes;
and
(d) the major achievements of the scheme towards improving the availability of healthcare
services, reducing out-of-pocket health expenditure for beneficiaries and achieving Universal
Health Coverage (UHC) in tribal and rural areas of the country?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) There has been a significant increase in the utilization of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan
Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) in Chhattisgarh, including Surguja district. The
number of Ayushman Cards created in the State increased from 3.18 lakh in FY 2018–19 to
14.52 lakh in FY 2025–26, while authorised hospital admissions increased from 3.42 lakh to
15.22 lakh during the same period, reflecting the growing outreach and utilization of the
Scheme by eligible beneficiaries.
As on 31.07.2026, a total of 2.47 crore Ayushman Cards have been created in the State,
including 8.49 lakh Ayushman Cards in Surguja district. Further, a total of 93.17 lakh hospital
admissions have been authorized in Chhattisgarh, of which 2.93 lakh hospital admissions
have been authorized in Surguja district.

(b): Under National Health Mission, through 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAM) in
the country, (including 5898 in Chhattisgarh State and 218 in Sarguja district),
comprehensive primary healthcare is provided by strengthening Sub Health Centres and
Primary Health Centres. These AAM provide preventive, promotive, rehabilitative and
curative care for an expanded range of services encompassing reproductive and child
healthcare services, communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and other health
issues.
(c): The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) was launched by the Government of
India in September 2021 to support the development of an integrated, citizen-centric national
digital health ecosystem. Several national health programme platforms, including
AB-PMJAY ,Nikshay, Reproductive and Child Health and Non-Communicable Disease are
integrated with ABDM. In addition, various government and private Hospital Management
Information System have also been integrated with ABDM, enabling these systems to create
Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA), create & share digital health records for
seamless interoperability across the ecosystem. The progress of ABDM, as on 31.07.2026 for
the country is as under:
 ABHA created for citizens – 95.99 crore
 Health Record Linked to citizen’s ABHA – 107.55 crore
 Verified Healthcare Professionals on Healthcare Professional Registry – 10.33 lacs
 Verified Health Facilities on Health Facility Registry- 5.40 lacs
 Facilities using ABDM-enabled software – 2.76 lacs
(d): AB-PMJAY has significantly improved access to quality secondary and tertiary
healthcare services for eligible beneficiaries through a nationwide network of empanelled
public and private hospitals. As on 31.07.2026, a total of 38,374 hospitals have been
empanelled under the scheme, across the country.
Further, more than 12.69 crore hospital admissions, amounting to more than Rs. 1.92 lakh
crore, have been authorized under the scheme, enabling eligible beneficiaries to avail
cashless treatment under the scheme.

(d) and (e): ‘Prisons and Prisoners’ is a State -list subject under Entry 4 of List II of the Seventh 
Schedule to the Constitution of India. Therefore, the administration and management of prisons 
and prisoners is the responsibility of respective State Governments. Central Government 
supplements the efforts of State Governments in this regard. Several initiatives are undertaken by 
the Central Government to operationalize bail reforms. Section 479 (1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) provides that “Where a person has, during the period of investigation, 
inquiry or trial under this Sanhita of an offence under any law (not being an offence for which 
the punishment of death or life imprisonment has been specified as one of the punishments under 
that law) undergone detention for a period extending up to one -half of the maximum period of 
imprisonment specified for that offence under that law, he shall be released by the Court on 
bail.”  Further, technology based alerts are generated through the ePrisons portal under Inter -
Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) and are sent to concerned officials for taking 
appropriate action for timely release of undertrial prisoners. 
 
With the objective of providing financial assistance to poor priso ners, who are unable to 
pay the fine imposed on them or are unable to secure bail due to financial constraints, the 
Government is implementing a scheme named  “Support to Poor Prisoners” . The guidelines and 
SOP for implementation of the Scheme,  has provision for  bail assistance amounting upto Rs. 1 
lakh, prescribing timelines for case processing, and simplif ication of procedures for drawal and 
utilisation of funds.  National Legal Services Authority (N ALSA) has taken initiatives for 
establishment of Under Trial Review Committees (UTRCs) in all the districts to recommend for 
release of eligible undertrial prisoners and convicts. Quarterly meetings are held by UTRCs 
across the country.

†3321. SHRI MURARI LAL MEENA: 
           
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the relatively disproportionate representation of 
various social categories, regions and women in the appointment of judges to the High Courts 
and the Supreme Court, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has consolidated data regarding the social category, gender and 
regional representation of judges in the High Courts and the Supreme Court, if so, the details

(c) whether the Government has conducted any study or consultation regarding the 
enhancement of the participation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward 
Classes, women and Economically Weaker Sections in the higher judiciary, if so, the key 
findings thereof; and 
(d) the policy steps being taken by the Government to promote transparency, equal opportunity 
and broader social representation in the higher judiciary? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY 
OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to (d): Appointment of Judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts is made under Articles 
124, 217 and 224 of the Constitution of India, which do not provide for reservation for any 
caste or class of persons. Therefore, category-wise data pertaining to representation of any caste 
or class of persons among the Judges of Supreme Court and the High Courts is not centrally 
available.  
 
As per the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP), the responsibility for initiation of 
proposals for appointment of Judges in the Supreme Court vests with the Chief Justice of India, 
while the responsibility for initiation of proposals for appointment of Judges in  High Courts 

2 
 
vests with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. However, the Government is 
committed to enhancing social diversity in judiciary and has been requesting the Chief Justices 
of High Courts that while sending proposals for appointment of Judges, due consideration be 
given to suitable candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward 
Classes, Minorities and Women to ensure social diversity in the appointment of Judges in High 
Courts. Only those persons who are recommended by th e Supreme Court Collegium, are 
appointed as Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3322 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 07.08.2026 
 
Uninterrupted availability of Fertilizers 
 
✝3322.  Shri Sanatan Pandey: 
           
 Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that farmers of Uttar Pradesh are facing 
problems related to availability, price rise and timely supply of fertilizers, if so, the 
details thereof, district-wise, particularly Ballia Lok Sabha Constituency; 
 
(b)  the details of fertilizer subsidy provided to farmers in respect of Uttar Pradesh, 
particularly in said Constituency during the last three years along with the current 
policy of pricing of fertilizers in the said district; 
 
(c) whether any special monitoring mechanism has been put in place by the 
Government in the said region to ensure uninterrupted availability of fertilizers, to 
prevent black marketing and to provide fertilizers to farmers at reasonable prices in 
the said district, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether any new project/scheme has been approved by the Government for 
expansion of chemical and fertilizer industry, investment promotion and employment 
generation in Uttar Pradesh; and 
 
(e)  if so, the details thereof and the current status of the same? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
____________________________________________________________________________ 
(a) to (e) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country, including the State of Uttar 
Pradesh: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 

adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
 
(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well 
in advance to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient 
rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
Accordingly, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS has remained 
adequate in Uttar Pradesh during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. The district-wise 
information regarding availability position of these fertilizers during the ongoing Kharif 
2026 season, as informed by the State, is placed at Annexure. 
 
Further, under 'DBT in Fertilizers' system, 100% subsidy on various fertilizer grades is 
released to the fertilizer companies, on actual sales to the beneficiaries based on Aadhar 
authentication through PoS devices installed at each retail shop. Accordingly, all farmers 
including those in the state of Uttar Pradesh are being supplied fertilizers at the subsidized 
rates on no-denial basis. The details of total fertilizer subsidy disbursed during the last 
three years i.e. 2023-24 to 2025-26 by the Government are given below: 
Figures in Rs. Crore 
Financial Year 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 
Amount disbursed 195420.51 177129.50 217175.73 
 
Further, under the Urea Subsidy Scheme, Urea is provided to the farmers at a 
statutorily notified Maximum Retail Price (MRP). The MRP of 45 kg bag of urea is Rs.242 
per bag (exclusive of charges towards neem coating and taxes as applicable). The 
difference between the delivered cost of urea at farm gate and net market realization by 
the urea units is given as subsidy to the urea manufacturer/importer by the Government 
of India. Accordingly, all farmers are being supplied urea at the subsidized rate. 
Further, the Government has implemented Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme w.e.f. 
01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. Under NBS Scheme, MRP of 
P&K fertilizers are decontrolled and companies are free to fix MRP as per their business 
dynamics at a reasonable level. The NBS subsidy is provided to manufacturer/importer 
on notified P&K fertilizers on its PoS sale during the season, depending on their nutrient 
content to ensure availability of fertilizers to farmers. The volatility in international prices 

of key fertilizers and raw materials is considered while fixing NBS rates for P&K fertilizers 
so that fertilizers remain affordable to the farmers. 
However, to make DAP being a key fertilizer, available at affordable price of Rs. 1350 per 
50 kg bag, special provisions like Rs. 3500 per MT to cover 'Other Costs' which includes 
costs incurred from factory gate to farm gate, advantage / disadvantage due to increase 
/ decrease in international prices, provision for GST component included in the MRP and 
provision for reasonable return @ 4% of net MRP (MRP-GST) have been extended to 
both imported and domestic DAP and imported TSP over and above NBS subsidy for 
Kharif 2026 season to keep the prices of fertilizers stable. 
Further, in order to address the issues of black-marketing and other malpractices, 
fertilizers are declared as an essential commodity under the Essential Commodities Act-
1955 and notified under Fertilizer Control Order- 1985. State Governments are 
adequately empowered to take action against persons involved in such malpractices, as 
per provisions of EC Act. The complaints received at D/o Fertilizers level regarding these 
malpractices are sent to concerned State Government to take appropriate action under 
Essential Commodities Act-1955 and Fertilizer Control Order-1985.  
As informed by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, 9,896 inspections are conducted 
and 36 FIRs have been registered against defaulters to curb black-marketing in the State 
of Uttar Pradesh during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. 
Furthermore, the Union Cabinet on 24.07.2026 approved the BHAVYA-
Rasayan (Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana-Rasayan) Scheme for establishing three 
dedicated Chemical Parks in the country, with a total budget outlay of Rs. 3,030 Crore 
under the Challenge Route. Under the Challenge Route, all States and Union Territories, 
including Uttar Pradesh, are eligible to apply for the establishment of a Chemical Park in 
accordance with the Scheme guidelines. Under the Scheme, the Central Government will 
provide financial assistance of up to Rs. 1,000 Crore for each Chemical Park, subject to 
a minimum contribution of Rs. 500 Crore by the respective State Government.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.  3323 
ANSWERED ON 07.08.2026  
  
CHILD CARE INSTITUTIONS  
 
3323.  SHRI K RADHAKRISHNAN:  
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
  
(a)  the number of registered Child Care Institutions functioning in the country, State-wise; 
(b)  whether the Government has conducted inspections of these institutions during the last 
three years, if so, the details of any violations detected therein;  
(c)  the details of the action taken against institutions found violating the provisions of the 
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015; and  
(d)  the details of the measures being taken to strengthen monitoring and ensure the safety, 
rehabilitation and welfare of children residing in such institutions  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR)  
 
  
(a) to (d) :  The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal Ministry for the 
administration of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act, 2015) 
which is the primary legislation for ensuring safety, security, dignity and well -being of 
children and is implemented by all the States and Union Territories. The Act creates statutory 
structures at the State and District levels which include State Child Protection Society, Child 
Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice Boards, District Child Protection Units. It also provides 
for establishment of Child Care Institutions (CCIs).  
  
Under the JJ Act 2015, the Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) have been empowered to take 
decisions with regard to the children in need of care and protection including orphaned, 
abandoned and surrendered children. They are also mandated to monitor the functi oning of 
the Child Care Institutions (CCIs). Similarly, the Juvenile Justice Boards (JJBs) are 
empowered to take decisions regarding the welfare of children in conflict with law. The Act 
defines standards of care and protection to secure the best interest of children living in CCIs 
and aims to provide family environment through non -institutional care services which 
includes sponsorship, foster care and aftercare.  
  
This Ministry is implementing Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely ‘Mission Vatsalya’ 
through the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations on pre -defined cost 
sharing basis between the Centre and the State Governments to deliver various services for 

children in difficult circumstances, which include both institutional and non -institutional care 
services.  
  
Under Section 54 of the JJ Act, 2015, the State Governments and UT Administrations appoint 
Inspection Committees to assess the basic facilities and infrastructure of the Institutions for 
maintaining their standards. Also, Sections 32 to 34 of JJ Act, 2015 mention the procedure for 
mandatory reporting including offence for non -reporting and penalty.  
  
The JJ Act, 2015 and Rules made thereunder provide for inspection of Child Care Institutions 
by State Level Inspection Committee and District Level Inspection Committee. The District 
Level Inspection Committee is constituted by the District Magistrate with  Additional District 
Magistrate as Chairperson. The District Level Inspection Committee inspects all CCIs in the 
district and submits the report of the findings to the District Magistrate or the State 
Government for improvement and development of CCIs in a ccordance with the provisions of 
the JJ Act, 2015 and Rules made thereunder. The District Magistrate being the focal point in 
the district for implementation of the Act, takes follow up action on the report of inspection 
committees and ensure that correcti ve measures are taken in a time bound manner.  
  
The Ministry of Women and Child Development has developed an integrated unified Mission 
Vatsalya Portal in consultation and coordination with States and UTs.  The TrackChild portal 
for Missing/Found Children, and Khoya -Paya application for Missing/Sighted C hildren have 
been integrated with this unified Mission Vatsalya Portal. The TrackChild  module of the 
Mission Vatsalya portal is implemented with support and involvement of various stakeholders 
namely Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Railways, State Governments and UT 
Administrations, Child Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice Boards, National Legal Services 
Authority, etc. Standard operating procedure have been issued in this regard. Advisories have 
also been issued to all States and UTs including Director General of Police of all States & UTs 
and other stakeholders regarding implementa tion of the portal. It is also integrated with the 
Crime and Criminal Tracking & Network Systems (CCTNS) of the Ministry of Home Affairs 
which allows interoperability in terms of matching of FIRs of missing children with data base 
of Mission Vatsalya Porta l to trace and match missing children by the State and UT police 
concerned. Further, through Khoya Paya module, any citizen can report about any missing or 
sighted child. 
  
The number of Child Care Institutions (CCIs) funded under Mission Vatsalya Scheme State 
and UT-wise during FY 2025-26 is at Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3324 
ANSWERED ON 07/08/2026 
KERALA AS GLOBAL HUB FOR AYURVEDA TOURISM 
 
3324. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL 
 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any special initiatives to promote Kerala as a 
global hub for Ayurveda and wellness tourism during the last five years; 
(b) if so, the details of the funds allocated and released to Kerala, scheme-wise; 
(c) the details of the research projects, Centres of Excellence, medicinal plant cultivation 
programmes and AYUSH institutions supported by the Central Government in the State; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to promote evidence -based Ayurveda, international 
accreditation and exports of Ayurvedic products from Kerala? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
(a) & (b)  The Government has adopted a comprehensive strategy to promote Ayush -based 
tourism in the country. Ministry of Tourism has formulated a National Strategy and Roadmap 
for Medical and Wellness Tourism in consultation with other Ministries including Ministry of 
Ayush. 
To facilitate international visitors seeking Ayush -based treatments, the Government 
introduced a separate category of Ayush Visa on 27 July 2023. Ministry of Ayush has also 
signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with India Tourism Development 
Corporation (ITDC), Ministry of Tourism to work together for the promotion of Medical 
Value Travel (MVT) in Ayurveda and other traditional systems of medicine.  So far, Ministry 
of Ayush has org anized two Medical Value Travel Summits, one for Western zone on 
30.09.2024 at Mumbai with participation of States/UTs of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, 
Goa, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, and the other for the Southern Zone on 
26.05.2025 at Chennai with participation of States/UTs like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, 
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Puducherry, with the aim of strengthening India’s position 
in Medical Value Travel. 
 
(c)  The research activities in the State are undertaken through the units/institutes under the 
respective Research Councils of the Ministry of Ayush. At present, 34 research programmes 
are being carried out at the National Homoeopathy Research Institute in Mental Health 

2 
 
(NHRIMH), Kottayam, which functions under the Central Council for Research in 
Homoeopathy (CCRH). Two institutes under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic 
Sciences (CCRAS) are functioning in the State of Kerala, namely the National Ayurveda 
Research Institute for Panchakarma (NARIP), Cheruthuruthy, and the Regional Ayurveda 
Research Institute (RARI), Thiruvananthapuram. CCRAS has undertaken various research 
projects in the State, including Medico -Ethno Botanical Surveys (MEBS), ethno -dietary 
studies, inventory of phytodiversity of medicinal plants, and programmes related to the 
cultivation of medicinal plants. The Clinical Research Unit of the Central Council for 
Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM) is functioning at Edathala, Kerala, and provides 
healthcare services across geriatric, reproductive, and non-communicable disease sectors. The 
Siddha Regional Research Institute (SRRI) functioning under the Central Council for 
Research in Siddha (CCRS), situated in Poojapura, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala is dedicated 
exclusively to research in Siddha medicine. The institute is actively involved in scientific 
validation of traditional Siddha formulations, evidence -based clinical studies, and 
standardization of Siddha medicines.  This institute engages in Intramural Research (IMR) 
projects on clinical research, Drug Standardization Research and Medicinal Plants Research. 
 Under the National A yush Mission (NAM), the Government of India extends 
financial assistance to the State of Kerala for strengthening Ayush healthcare services 
through the State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs), which are approved annually in accordance 
with the provisions of the NAM Operational Guidelines. The support provided under NAM 
includes both recurring and non -recurring grants. Recurring grants cover the supply of 
medicines and contingencies to Ayush institutions, as well as human resource support for 
Ayush hospitals. Non -recurring grants include infrastructure development such as 
construction, renovation, upgradation and strengthening of Ayush healthcare facilities, along 
with the provision of equipment and furniture for Ayush institutions. 
 Under the ‘Conservation, Development and Sustainable Managem ent of Medicinal 
Plants’ a Central Sector Scheme implemented by National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), 
Ministry of A yush, project based financial support is provided for research activities on 
various aspects of medicinal plants to government as well as private universities/research 
institutions/organizations across the country. The details are at Annexure I. 
 Under Ayurswasthya Yojana, a Central Sector Scheme, implemented by Ministry of 
Ayush, two Centres of Excellence (CoE)  projects have been approved in Kerala. The details 
are at Annexure II. 
 
 (d) The Government has taken the following steps to promote evidence -based Ayurveda, 
international accreditation, and exports of Ayurvedic products, including from Kerala:

ii. Ayush Standard Mark and Ayush Pre mium Mark are awarded to Ayush d rugs by 
Quality Council of India (QCI) based on third -party assessment of compliance with 
prescribed national and international quality standards respectively.  Ayush Quality 
Mark Programme was launched in 2025 by the Ministry of Ayush to strengthen 

3 
 
quality assurance, enhance consum er confidence, and improve the g lobal recognition 
and competitiveness of Ayush products and services.  Over the years 77 Ayush 
healthcare organizations in Kerala are accredited by National Accreditation Board for 
Hospitals (NABH), a constituent board of the QCI. 
iii. Ayurveda and Yoga have  been included under Sectional Commit tee 2 of ISO/TC249 
to focus on international s tandards of Ayurveda and Yoga, terminology, quality and 
safety of ingredients, extrac ts, finished products, Ayurveda -based dietary 
supplements, Yoga accessories etc. 
iv. As reported by the Government of Kerala, a 14 -member Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani 
(ASU) Standardization Committee has been constituted under the chairmanship of the 
Principal Secretary, Dept. of Ayush. The Committee has been tasked to examine the 
various challenges faced by the ASU drug manufacturing industry, to suggest 
practical solutions, and mak e recommendations for improving standardization across 
the sector.  As part of its mandate, the Committee organized a one -day stakeholder 
workshop on 15 February 2024, bringing together representatives from the Ayurveda 
drug manufacturing industry and other relevant stakeholders. The workshop 
facilitated the identification of existing issues and explored feasible corrective 
measures for strengthening quality assurance and regulatory compliance.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF AYUSH  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3325    
ANSWERED ON 07/08/2026 
 
ADOPTION OF AYUSH GRID IN NABARANGPUR, ODISHA 
 
3325. Shri Balabhadra Majhi  
 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of the progress made in the implementation of various digital platforms and e -
Governance tools, including the AYUSH Grid and My AYUSH Integrated Services Portal, 
and their implementation in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency of Odisha; 
 
(b) the extent to which the AYUSH Grid has been adopted by States, Union Territories and  
health institutions and its impact on healthcare delivery in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary  
Constituency of Odisha; and 
 
(c) the details of the Government's roadmap for the further digital transformation of the  
AYUSH Grid and its integration with national health programmes, including the measures  
proposed for the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency, Odisha? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH  
 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV)  
 
(a) The Ayush Grid  project serves as the IT backbone of the Ayush sector, driving digital 
transformation across healthcare, research & development, Ayush drug administration, 
medicinal plants, education & awareness, capacity building and global/media outreach.   
Under this initiative, twenty -four e -governance platforms have been developed and made 
accessible across the country. The My Ayush Integrated Services Portal (MAISP), the master 
portal of the Ministry of Ayush  available at https://www.maisp.ayush.gov.in , integrates all 
Ayush-related applications and services into a unified digital ecosystem. An AI -enabled 
chatbot (Beta version) has also been deployed to assist visitors and enhance user experience. 
The portal facilitates citizen-centric access to various services and schemes and enables real -
time monitoring and data-driven decision-making. (Details available at: maisp.ayush.gov.in)  
Similarly, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) -compliant Ayush Hospital 
Management Information System (AHMIS) has been deployed to digitize healthcare delivery 

and improve the management of Ayush health facilities. The Ayush Anudan Portal has 
streamlined the submission, processing, approval, and monitoring of funding proposals under 
various Central Sector Schemes of the Ministry. The Ayush Research Portal serves as a 
centralized digital repository of over 43,000 curated Ayush research publications, facilitating 
easy access for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers. The Ayush Nivesh Saarthi Portal 
serves as a dedicated gateway for domestic and international investors in the Ayush sector, 
providing comprehensive information to promote investment opportunities. The e -Charak 
portal functions as a virtual marketplace and information platform for the medicinal plants 
sector, connecting farmers, collectors, buyers, manufacturers, and exporters. 
The Y -Break Pro mobile application promotes holistic well -being in workplaces through 
short Yoga sessions. The mYoga application encourages regular Yoga practice by providing 
learning modules and guided sessions that can be accessed anytime and anywhere.  The Yoga 
Portal serves as a dedicated digital platform for promoting Yoga as a holistic lifestyle practice 
and enhancing its accessibility to all. It provides authentic and structured information on 
Yoga protocols, training modules, certified institutions, events, and research studies, ensuring 
credibility and ease of access for learners and practitioners. 
Further, Yoga Sangam , hosted on the Yoga Portal during the  International Day of Yoga 
(IDY) 2026 , witnessed the registration of over  7.6 lakh organizations  across the country . 
Among these,  441 organizations  were registered from the  Nabarangpur Parliamentary 
Constituency of Odisha , indicating active participation  from the constituency in the 
nationwide Yoga celebration. 
Collectively, all e -governance tools developed under the Ayush Grid are accessible to 
everyone and have strengthened service de livery, improved operational efficiency, and 
enhanced transparency and accountability. 
(b) The Ayush Grid has improved access to Ayush -based primary healthcare, including in 
rural and aspirational districts, by strengthening digital infrastructure and standardizing 
service delivery.  
Through platforms such as the Ayush Hospital Management Information System (A -HMIS), 
patient registration, electronic health records, referrals and continuity of care are being 
enabled digitally. As on 31st July 2026, a total of 6,245 Ayush health facilities across the 
country have been onboarded onto AHMIS . Regional Research Institute in Unani Medicine , 
Regional Research Institute in Homoeopathy and Central Ayurveda Research Institute have 
on-boarded on AHMIS application in Odisha. Real-time dashboards and standardized 
reporting further support monitoring, planning and targeted interventions by State and 
District authorities, thereby enhancing availability and accessibility of Ayush services in such 
areas.  
Further, the PM GatiShakti portal has enabled GIS mapping of Ayush health facilities using 
PM Gatishakti Ayush Asset Mapping Tool to support planning and decision -making. As on 
15 July 2026, a total of 6,002 facilities have been mapped on the portal  among which 85 
Standalone Ayush dispensaries and 150 AAMs are from Odisha State . In Yoga Sangam  
hosted on Yoga Portal during International Day of Yoga 2026 , 441 organizations have been 
registered under Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency of Odisha. 

The adoption of these digital platforms by Ayush healthcare institutions across States and 
Union Territories has enhanced the accessibility, quality, and continuity of Ayush services, 
including rural and aspirational districts. 
(c) Ministry of Ayush is strengthening the Ayush Grid as a comprehensive digital ecosystem 
for the Ayush sector by enhancing digital platforms, promoting interoperability, adopting 
emerging technologies like Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, and enabling data -
driven governance.  
These efforts are aimed at improving service delivery, facilitating evidence -based 
policymaking, providing multilingual support in convergence with Digital India BHASHINI 
Division (DIBD) under Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), and 
ensuring seamless integration with national health programmes and digital health initiatives, 
including the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).
